item.title: 29-year-old Nigerian man killed as tree crushes car in London
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 29-year-old Nigerian man, James Abiwon, has died after a tree fell on his car during Storm Boelo in Mill Hill, north London. According to Metro UK, Abiwon was driving along Dollis Road at about 12.30pm on Sunday when the tree came down in strong winds. Emergency crews, including police officers, firefighters, paramedics and an air ambulance, responded, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. His cousin, Tyrrell Okolo, described him as “a master of everything” and a devoted family man. Abiwon was a tech sales executive who had earned a degree from the University of Essex. He was also a semi-professional footballer with Aldershot, a musician with about 40,000 YouTube viewers and a mentor to many, his cousin said. Abiwon had been preparing to celebrate his 30th birthday with a padel tournament. The event will now go ahead in his memory, with proceeds going to support his family. His close friend, Kwame Affum, 29, said the two had played padel together just two days before the crash. “I’m trying hard to get my head around this,” he told Metro UK. A friend had messaged Abiwon shortly before the accident about money they owed him for the court, but he did not reply, prompting concern. Affum said Abiwon loved sport, was a good footballer and supported Arsenal. He had earned a first-class university degree and recently won an award at work. “He was full of energy and talent,” Affum said. “He was going to celebrate his 30th birthday in two weeks. It just seems impossible this has happened.” A witness who laid flowers at the scene told Metro UK that she heard a helicopter and went outside to find the fallen tree covering the road, with the car trapped beneath it. Abiwon’s girlfriend and best friend arrived while rescuers were still at the scene. The witness said they were shaking as they waited and hoped he would be brought out. The witness said Abiwon’s aunties and other relatives arrived later and were inconsolable. She described him as clearly well loved and said the community had lost one of its own. Traffic on Dollis Road was reportedly heavy at the time, as roadworks on a nearby street had diverted more vehicles onto the route. A neighbour whose home overlooks the scene said: “If it had been 10 minutes later, it could have been me.” The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to Dollis Road at about 12.40pm on Sunday after reports that a tree had fallen onto a moving car. Police are working with the local authority and coroner to establish the circumstances surrounding Abiwon’s death. Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 84mph across parts of the UK over the weekend. A 60-year-old man was also killed by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, while others were injured. item.title: Flamingos’ World Cup Form Offers Hope For Super Falcons’ Future
item.description: Nigeria’s impressive run at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco is offering hope for the future of the Super Falcons as the senior team faces the challenge of transitioning from an established generation to a new crop of players. The Flamingos have reached the quarter-finals after recovering from an opening 2-1 defeat to Poland, beating Puerto Rico 2-0 and defending champions North Korea 3-1 before overcoming Mexico 2-1 in the Round of 16 on Thursday. Goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Mary Dunstan secured the victory over Mexico, sending Nigeria into a quarter-final clash against Venezuela on Sunday, November 1. Mary Dunstan celebrates her goal for Flamingos against Mexico. X/@FIFAWWC Beyond their pursuit of a World Cup title, the Flamingos’ performances have offered a glimpse of what Nigeria’s next generation could bring to the senior women’s team. A Generation Showing Promise The need to prepare new players has become increasingly important for the Super Falcons following the departure of experienced internationals. Nigeria’s failure to defend its Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in 2026 has also renewed attention on the team’s future. Youth teams are designed partly to prepare players for senior international football, but the transition is rarely straightforward. Excelling at U-17 level does not guarantee success against older, more experienced opponents. For Nigeria, therefore, the Flamingos’ progress represents an encouraging starting point rather than a guarantee of future success. Flamingos. Photo credit: FIFA Their response to adversity has been particularly noteworthy. After losing to Poland, they bounced back against Puerto Rico before producing one of their biggest statements of the tournament by defeating North Korea, a two-time champion. According to FIFA records, North Korea had gone 2,900 days without a defeat in regulation time at the U-17 Women’s World Cup. Its last such loss came against Germany on November 14, 2018, when it was beaten 4-1. Nigeria ended that run with a commanding 3-1 victory. Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Rodiat Yusuf scored for the Flamingos, while North Korea managed a late consolation from the penalty spot. The result demonstrated Nigeria’s ability to compete against established youth teams. Their subsequent victory over Mexico has reinforced that impression, although the quarter-final against Venezuela will provide another test. Players To Watch Captain Harmony Chidi leads a squad that has produced several encouraging performances. In attack, Adegbuyi and Umejiaku have scored important goals, with Umejiaku also finding the net against Mexico. Yusuf has contributed creatively and scored a free-kick against North Korea, while Dunstan has also made her mark with goals in the tournament. Tosin Rafiu has contributed to the team’s attacking play, while defenders Azeezat Oduntan, Ohunene Sunday and Esther Stephen have featured in Nigeria’s efforts to contain opponents. item.title: AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale gives Ruben Amorim unconditional backing and insists Scudetto is '100% possible'
item.description: AC Milan v Atalanta BC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport RedBird Capital chief Gerry Cardinale has broken his silence on the current state of AC Milan, offering a ringing endorsement of manager Ruben Amorim. Despite a turbulent start to the campaign, the American owner remains convinced that the foundations for long-term success are firmly in place at San Siro. Cardinale clarifies stance on Ruben Amorim The hierarchy at Milan has moved to dispel any rumors regarding the job security of Amorim, with owner Cardinale offering his full support to the Portuguese tactician. Following a summer of significant change, the Rossoneri have experienced a mixed run of form that led to external questions about the direction of the project. However, Cardinale has stepped in to ensure that the internal belief in Amorim’s methods remains as high as it was on the day he was appointed to lead the club into a new era. Speaking candidly about the managerial situation, the RedBird founder emphasized that the club is not looking for short-term fixes but rather a sustainable path to the top of European football. "I have full faith in him. At the end of Top Gun, 'my' film, there's a great line: 'I'm not leaving my wingman', Tom Cruise says. And I'm not leaving Ruben. He is in no danger whatsoever. I will stand by his side. I won't make the mistakes made in recent years. He is my manager and we'll keep working together until we manage to make the step up.,” Cardinale told La Gazzetta dello Sport . Scudetto remains the primary objective Despite currently trailing the pace-setters in the Serie A standings, Cardinale is refusing to temper his expectations for the current season. The American businessman dismissed suggestions that this might be a transition year for the club, instead doubling down on the ambition to bring the league title back to the red and black side of Milan. He views the competitive nature of the league as an opportunity rather than a hurdle, believing the squad is deep enough to compete. "It is entirely possible, 100%. And I say that without wanting to sound arrogant. I wake up every morning hoping for a small opening, meaning Inter start drawing instead of winning and we start stringing together a run of wins. Winning is the only thing that matters to me, but let's take it one match at a time, gaining ground on those ahead of us, matchday by matchday,” Cardinale stated firmly. A new home to fight financial giants Beyond the pitch, the "Generali Stadium" project remains a top priority for RedBird. Cardinale views a new San Siro as a vital milestone for both the club and Italian football to compete with the financial might of the Premier League. "It's a project we've been working on for four years, a priority. The new San Siro is a key milestone for Italy, a country where it seemed impossible to build new facilities. item.title: 'Some of the things hurt me': Zimbabwe captain slams players' 'complacency' after series loss as Afghanistan go from 5 for 4 to score 221
item.description: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza was left disappointed with what he called "complacency" among some of his teammates after his side suffered a 19-run defeat to Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The loss also handed Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Raza said his biggest concern was the attitude of some players after Zimbabwe had reduced Afghanistan to 5 for 4 in the fourth over. He felt the team had taken the opposition lightly at that stage, assuming Afghanistan would struggle to post a big total. "For me, before I go too much in detail [about the match] - and I will address that in the changing room - the toughest part to swallow was the complacency that I saw from some of the boys," Raza said after the match. The Zimbabwe captain was particularly unhappy that some players appeared to believe Afghanistan would manage only 130 or 140 runs after losing four wickets early. He said the team needed to stay focused and remember that a match is not over until the final ball. "[At 5 for 4] some of the boys were probably calculating that it will be - 130, 140 max - at the end of 20 overs. Some of the things that I saw on the ground today certainly hurt me and I'll address that in the changing room because, listen, it can happen but I think that's where you have to be mentally very strong and say, 'no, the game is never over until it's over - we still have a job in hand and I'm going to be the guy who's going to get the job done'. "Before I dissect the game with batting or bowling, I think that's something that I felt today out there in the middle and that's something that needs to be addressed, not to take this game for granted because it can bite back and today is a great example." Zimbabwe had also kept Afghanistan to 45 for 5 at the halfway stage of the innings. However, Azmatullah Omarzai's 116 off 50 balls and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai's 52 off 27 deliveries helped Afghanistan recover and post 221 for 7. Raza then led Zimbabwe's fightback with an unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, but his effort was not enough to prevent defeat. He said he had tried to keep his emotions under control while batting after being unhappy with the team's approach in the first innings. "When you're chasing 222, for me the biggest thing was to try and stay in control of my emotions because the way we conducted ourselves in the first innings hurt me," Raza said. "So when we go out to bat, for me it was trying to win the game from any position. That has been our motto and in my head, I was just calculating how best can I go about my business and hopefully the other batters chip in so that we can win the game. "Up until the last two overs [by when they needed 46 from 12], we were backing ourselves to win the game but yeah, I think we left ourselves too much." Raza also said he would address the issue with his teammates in the dressing room, making it clear that his message would be stronger than what he had said publicly. 135358996

item.title: Roma among clubs interested in Lisandro Martinez
item.description: Roma among clubs interested in Lisandro Martinez Roma are also looking to England to strengthen their defense. Among the names linked to the Giallorossi is Lisandro Martinez, the Argentine center-back from Manchester United, whose future at Old Trafford appears increasingly uncertain. The 1998-born player’s contract expires in June 2027 and could leave the Red Devils at the end of the season following tensions in recent weeks with the English club. According to Spanish newspaper AS , Barcelona and Atlético Madrid are closely monitoring the defender’s situation, but they aren’t the only clubs interested. Roma, Inter Milan, and Como have also reportedly included Martinez among the options to evaluate for next summer.

item.title: Sam Altman sympathizes with mathematicians, but says OpenAI’s math onslaught won’t stop
item.description: After months of bombarding mathematicians with a relentless stream of AI-generated results, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he sympathizes with researchers struggling to make sense of it all. But he has no intention of stopping - and hints there could be much more to come from the company's stockpile of discoveries. "I think, on net, the world deserves to understand how the universe works," Altman said during an episode of the Cheeky Pint podcast released Thursday. "But I do have empathy for the method." item.title: Ohio State gets another shot at flipping top running back target
item.description: It’s been an interesting recruiting cycle for Ohio State at the running back position, and with the 2027 class still without a commitment at the spot, the Buckeyes are continuing to work toward changing that. Carlos Locklyn and the staff have certainly put in the effort, but the results haven’t gone their way to this point. After seeing top target David Gabriel-Georges choose Tennessee, Ohio State was dealt another tough blow last week when in-state prospect Jordan Hall committed to Penn State. With two of their top options now off the board, it’s fair to wonder where Ohio State turns next. The transfer portal remains an option, and many have assumed that’s the direction the Buckeyes will ultimately take. However, the coaching staff isn’t ready to throw in the towel on the high school recruiting trail just yet, and Thursday brought some encouraging news regarding a familiar name. Per Rivals, Gainesville, Georgia running back Nigel Newkirk has officially scheduled a visit to Columbus for Nov. 7, when Ohio State hosts Oregon. The Alabama commit has been on the Buckeyes’ radar for quite some time, and while his pledge to the Crimson Tide back in May appeared to put an end to Ohio State’s pursuit, Locklyn and the staff have continued to maintain contact. Clearly, that persistence is beginning to pay off. Getting Newkirk back on campus is a significant development for Ohio State, especially considering where things currently stand at the position. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound back is the No. 226 player nationally and the No. 16 running back in the 2027 class according to the 247Sports Composite rankings, and would be a major addition to a class that could certainly use some good news at running back. Of course, getting a committed prospect to visit and actually convincing him to flip are two very different things. Alabama won’t be eager to let Newkirk go, and Ohio State will still have plenty of work to do if it hopes to change his mind. Still, the opportunity to get him on campus for a marquee Big Ten matchup is about as good of a setting as the staff could ask for. The Buckeyes have had their share of frustrations recruiting running backs in this cycle, but they’re proving that they aren’t done fighting for the talent they want. Locklyn and company now have a legitimate opportunity to make up some ground, and the next step will be making sure Newkirk leaves Columbus with plenty to think about. item.title: Hansi Flick talks signing a new center-back and Barcelona’s defensive problems
item.description: Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images | Europa Press via Getty Images Barcelona’s defensive issues came into focus in their high-profile losses to PSG and Real Madrid last week, and talks of a new center-back signing have already started as we approach the January transfer window. Reports from Spanish media in the last 24 hours universally agree that Hansi Flick wants a new addition at the back this winter, and the coach pretty much confirmed that in a press conference on Friday. Flick also explained the root of the defensive issues in El Clásico , and focused on the importance of keeping the ball well and pressing from the front in addition to winning duels at the back. “I said it during the transfer window, we always talk about what’s best for the team, how we can improve it. It’s something we’re working on. We’ll see. We have a few weeks left before the transfer window opens. We’ve discussed it with Deco, Bojan, and my staff. That’s how we do things. If we can, maybe we will. “Ultimately, defending isn’t just the defenders’ job; even the striker defends. Everyone is involved. To begin with, we can’t lose the ball easily. We lost possession a few times against Real Madrid, which isn’t good. It’s something that happens to us often, and we need to play more intelligently, more focused. “When we’re defending in our own area, it’s also important to mark our opponents well, and we didn’t do that either. We have to improve in these situations. We train it, we take it into account, and we talk about it with the players.” I’ll believe it when I see it regarding the signing of a world-class center-back, something Barça have lacked since Iñigo Martínez left. But it’s at least good to see the clear intention from Flick and Deco to solve a pretty glaring issue when it comes to Barça’s ability to win the biggest games.

item.title: What did you think of the World Series?
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 28: Cooper Pratt #12 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates with the Commissioner's Trophy during the trophy presentation alongside teammates after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 to win in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 28, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The World Series is over, and we’ve all had a day to sit with the result. The Milwaukee Brewers have been crowned champions for the first time in their history, and they did it through a very impressive run through the postseason after being the best team in the regular season. It may have appeared a fait accompli to some, as anyone closely watching this Brewers team could tell they were a juggernaut. But sometimes it’s entertaining to watch a great team simply be great, proving over and over again that they are indeed the best team in baseball for a given year. This World Series may not have been the seven game thriller last year’s series was, but it still had some great moments. The highlights of course being Milwaukee’s legendary eight run rally with two outs in the fifth inning of Game 3 and the Rays’ walk-off win to cap off a 12-inning epic. Nevertheless, it would be fair to feel a little disappointed with how quickly the series ended after all the hype of the two top seeds facing off set in. In any case, it was the last MLB games we’ll see for at least six months, or possibly longer with the 2027 season fully up in the air due to the incoming lockout. So, what did you think of this year’s World Series? Did it live up to your expectations? Or were you a little disappointed?

item.title: Villanova vs Notre Dame: Game Preview
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 07: Head coach Micah Shrewsberry of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish looks on during the ACC basketball tip off at Hilton Charlotte Uptown on October 07, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images Villanova Wildcats (0-0) vs Notre Dame Fighting Irish (0-0) Where : Palazzo dello Sport (Rome, Italy) When: Sunday, November 1 at 9:30 AM EST Betting Line: Villanova -7.5 (subject to change) How to Watch: FOX How to Listen : Villanova Sports Radio Network KenPom: Villanova 32, Notre Dame 83 Torvik: Villanova 30, Notre Dame 81 Evan Miya : Villanova 30, Notre Dame 83 About Notre Dame : Micah Shrewsberry, the former Penn State head coach, is going into his fourth season with Notre Dame. Shrewsberry took over for Mike Brey, who coached the team for the previous 23 years. Brey had this program nationally relevant more often than not throughout his tenure, but that has yet to be the case for Shrewsberry. In his final season with Penn State, Shrewsberry led the Nittany Lions to an NCAA-Tournament birth and a second round game against No. 2 Texas, coming up just short in a 71-66 loss. The expectations were that he would parlay that into success with Notre Dame, but through three seasons his combined record is 41-56. Things are not expected to go any better this year for the Fighting Irish, as they were picked to finish 16th in an 18-team ACC. Notre Dame had no players selected for preseason honors. The only two programs selected to finish behind the Fighting Irish were Boston College and Georgia Tech, both of whom have new coaches. Notre Dame played two exhibition games, both away from home. The first game came at Dayton, where Notre Dame fell 75-65. In the second contest, the Fighting Irish took down fellow Big East team DePaul 71-63. Notre Dame’s leading scorer in the Dayton game was Penn transfer Ethan Roberts, who Villanova fans should be familiar with over the past two seasons. Roberts averaged 16.9 points, three rebounds and 3.9 assists per game for the Quakers a year ago, and he projects as a potential leading scorer for Notre Dame this season. He was the only player in double-figures on the night with 11. In the contest with DePaul, starting center Logan Duncomb missed the game with a leg injury. Listed as day-to-day, the expectation is that the 6’10” senior will be available against Villanova. Duncomb is a senior transfer from Winthrop who averaged 18.3 points and 8.9 rebounds per game. The leading scorers in the game against the Blue Demons were Brady Koehler with 19, Braeden Smith with 17 and Jonathan Sanderson with 13. Koehler is a 6’10” sophomore who averaged 5.6 points per game in his freshman year for Notre Dame. He is a capable three-point shooter for his height, having made 4/10 in the exhibition games. Smith, a 6’ senior transfer from Gonzaga, averaged 5.1 points per game for the Bulldogs a year ago. Smith played his first two seasons at Colgate, averaging 11.6 and 12.

item.title: Siena basketball coach Nevada Smith treats student managers to dinner
item.description: Siena men's basketball coach Nevada Smith, front left, took the team's student managers out to dinner at Beer Bones Bar & Grill in Latham on Wednesday before the Saints open at Bryant next Monday. (Courtesy of Nevada Smith) LOUDONVILLE - It was a team outing of sorts, except without the players. New Siena men's basketball coach Nevada Smith took nine of his student managers to dinner on Wednesday at Beer Bones Bar & Grill in Latham. Only one manager on vacation was missing. "Just had some wings, got to watch some sports," senior Fen Egan of Mechanicville said. "Just connect and have a good time." It was Smith's way of saying thanks to the students who handle the behind-the-scenes tasks for the Saints, who open their season Monday against Bryant in Smithfield, R.I. "We do that at the beginning of the year, every year," Smith, a former Marquette assistant, said. "Just an appreciation for them so they understand how important they are to our organization. Everything they do helps us, helps every guy on our team. I think we have the best managing group in the country. I'd put them up against anyone. They're hard-working. They're intelligent. They understand what we're looking for." On a college basketball team, student managers handle everything from setting up equipment, to handing out towels and water bottles, to assisting in workouts. At the beginning of Thursday's practice, Egan, a former Mechancville guard, and other managers took part in halfcourt drills. "Same thing with the players, whatever it takes to win," Egan said. "Everybody's got a job and it's important that everybody does their job at the highest level possible." Siena has 10 student managers to assist the coaching staff and 16 players on the roster. The Saints listed four managers last season under former head coach Gerry McNamara. "We wouldn't bring someone in that wasn't a great fit for us," Smith said. "We wouldn't bring someone in who didn't bring value for our program. They all do such a great job with our guys. We live a lot in individual workouts and we need a lot of guys around the gym. They're a huge part of what we do and how we do it." Egan said every coach he's served under - Carmen Maciariello, McNamara and Smith - has treated the managers very well. "Every staff gives us a lot of opportunity," Egan said. "It's just a gift to be able to come and learn from them, and from the players, and just have that family relationship." Coyle gaining strength Smith said he thinks graduate forward Brendan Coyle of Niskayuna will be available for Monday's opener. Coyle missed the Oct. 18 exhibition loss to Syracuse with an upper-body injury. Coyle was dressed and participating at the start of Thursday's practice. "He's starting to come back full strength," Smith said. "We're excited to see where we can be when he's at full strength. We really haven't had that yet. He's a guy that we look to to calm us down, make some plays, that understands what winning at the highest level looks like

item.title: Patriots vs. Dolphins predictions: Pats get back on track in Week 8
item.description: After enjoying a weekend off, the New England Patriots are back in action this Sunday. Their opponent coming out of the mini-bye is a familiar one, at least on paper: the Miami Dolphins. However, these are not the same Dolphins that lost both of their games to the Patriots in 2025. Led by new head coach Jeff Hafley, they have overhauled significant portions of their roster and staff. Are they better off as a result? So far, the record doesn’t say so. That said, unlike the Patriots, the Dolphins are entering Week 8 off a victory — their first of the season. Still, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Patriots are seen as seven-point favorites entering the game. Will they live up to that status? Or will the Dolphins manage to defend their home turf? Let’s find out what Pats Pulpit’s staff and community think. Patriots vs. Dolphins score predictions Bernd Buchmasser: The Dolphins are not as bad as their 1-5 record would suggest, but they still have some shortcomings across the board and are simply a less talented team than their opponent this week. Even a shorthanded Patriots team playing on the road should therefore be able to come away victoriously, especially after 10 days of rest. Anything else would be a major cause for concern for a team with serious playoff aspirations. | Patriots 28, Dolphins 10 Patriots fans, join the game-day huddle! item.title: They played for Celtic – Peter Wilson
item.description: They played for Celtic – Peter Wilson Ayrshire born Peter Wilson signed for Celtic in May 1923 from hometown side Beith, and would go on to represent the hoops for eleven years as well as winning four caps for Scotland… Peter Wilson Celtic FC. Image by Celtic Curio for Celtic in the Thirties by Matt Corr The talented right half would make his debut on 16th February 1924 in a 1-0 league win over Motherwell at Fir Park. His job that day was to mark the Steelmen’s talented winger Bob Ferrier, one of the best and most feared players of his day in the Scottish game, yet Peter Wilson equipped himself well as he helped Celtic to a much deserved victory and also a clean sheet. Peter was an exceptional passer of the ball, and had a terrific footballing brain, he was always one step ahead in his thinking as he set up attacks for the Hoops over his time at Celtic. Peter Wilson, Celtic FC. Photo The Celtic Wiki It was once said of the Celtic right-half: “Peter Wilson didn’t pass the ball, he stroked it“. He was certainly heralded as a very fine player, and was said to have a “cool style“, “easy-oasy“, and was a “carpet artist”. Unfortunately for Peter, Rangers were the dominant side in that era, and he would win just one solitary league winners medal, although his luck in the Scottish Cup was much better as he picked up four winners medals (1925, 1927, 1931 and 1933). Peter Wilson, Celtic FC. Photo The Celtic Wiki It was something of a bleak era for the club, but Peter was one of the players exempt from criticism, a testament to the ability he possessed, with the league title winning season 1925/26 regarded as his most productive campaign, with the accomplished Jimmy McStay and John Mcfarlane beside him in the Celtic defence. Celtic 1930/31. Back; Willie Cook, Peter Kavanagh, Hugh Smith & Peter Wilson. Middle; Peter McGonagle, Chic Geatons, Denis O’Hare, John Thomson, Bobby Whitelaw, Willie Hughes & Will Quinn (Trainer). Front; Bertie Thomson, Alec Thomson, Jimmy McGrory, Jimmy McStay, Peter Scarff & Charlie Napier. Photo Celtic in the Thirties by Matt Corr After making 395 appearances and scoring 15 goals in an 11 year career in the famous green and white hoops, Peter would leave the club and sign for the Ggreen and white of Hibernian in the summer of 1934. Peter perhaps didn’t achieve the recognition that some of his more ‘popular’ teammates such as Patsy Gallagher, Tommy McInally, and Jimmy McGrory received, but he was very much a valued member of the Celtic side of that particular era. You can read more about Peter Wilson in Matt Corr’s outstanding Celtic in the Thirties with both volumes available from Celtic Star Books. While in the city they were given a tour of the famous Ford Motor Works. L – R: Willie Cook, Bobby Whitelaw, Hugh Smith, Joe McGhee, Willie Maley, Bertie Thomson, Johnny Thomson, Jimmy

item.title: How Injuries Hit Pro Marathoners in the Wallet
item.description: About two and a half weeks before she was due to line up at Sunday’s New York City Marathon, elite runner Fiona O’Keeffe had to share a change of plans . Instead of racing through the five boroughs on Sunday, she’d be recovering from surgery to repair a fully retracted tendon tear in her hamstring. Though they work hard to stay healthy, injury is a fact of life for elite marathoners, who often log upward of 100 miles weekly. “A lot of these folks, they’re dealing with something at all times,” Dr. Efren Caballes, a sports medicine physician in Colorado who treats both professional and recreational endurance athletes, tells Front Office Sports . “It’s just a matter of, how often does it start to limit their training?” These setbacks are physically and emotionally challenging for any elite athlete. For professional marathoners, they can also be expensive. O’Keeffe placed fourth and set the American course record of 2:22:49 in NYC last year, earning $50,000 in prize money . Withdrawing means she misses her chance to compete for her share of this year’s $969,000 purse . And athletes who don’t make it to the starting line typically forfeit all the appearance fees offered by World Marathon Majors and other big races, agent Hawi Keflezighi tells FOS. (He doesn’t represent O’Keeffe, but has several clients in Sunday’s race, including Zouhair Talbi and Annie Frisbie. Appearance deals are individually negotiated and typically confidential.) In 2025, pro runner Lindsay Flanagan had to scratch from three marathons she’d committed to: Boston, Chicago, and Valencia. The money she lost in appearance fees would have at least doubled her income from her base contract and coaching, and if she’d performed well, she could have earned even more in prize money and bonuses. “We don’t do it for the money, but at the same time, this is how I pay my mortgage,” she tells FOS . “It’s my job. I think it would be crazy if I wasn’t upset about that.” The Cost of Care To add to the strain, many pro runners bear the brunt of their own healthcare costs. Professional sports leagues like the NFL, NBA, and WNBA have collective bargaining agreements governing areas like pay, working conditions, and healthcare coverage. Pro runners, meanwhile, operate as independent contractors without such protections, agent Josh Cox tells FOS . Runners’ primary sponsorships typically come from footwear companies, and with rare exceptions, these deals don’t include health insurance, Cox says. Some brands include a line item in contracts to cover premiums, Keflezighi says, while others have team setups that offer support. For example, a training group might have a physical therapist or other health professional on staff, or offer access to other recommended providers, with some or all costs paid for out of a team budget. And nearly all shoe contracts have a line item for massage, physical therapy, and similar expenses, Keflezighi says. However, insurance doesn’t typically cover some newer treatments th

item.title: NFL Predictions: Can the Bears’ defense slow down the Seahawks’ offense?
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 26: Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks is tackled by safety Jonathan Owens #36 of the Chicago Bears during the third quarter of an NFL football game, at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images A Monday Night Football matchup between the Chicago Bears and the Seattle Seahawks is a circle-the-calendar game that NFL fans got excited about on schedule release day. Those games don’t always feel quite as big once the season gets rolling, but this one gets the full court press of hype (even more so with each team making a big-time trade). The (5-2) Bears are coming off a prime-time win over the New England Patriots, and the (4-3) Seahawks are coming off a prime-time win over the Kansas City Chiefs. These are two legit Super Bowl contenders. Ben Johnson’s Bears have one of the NFL’s most explosive offenses, and Mike Macdonald’s Seahawks again have one of the league’s most suffocating defenses, but this game might come down to the other side of the ball. Can Chicago’s defense slow down a Seahawks offense with a refocused rushing attack and one of the game’s best wide receivers, Jaxon Smith-Njigba? The Bears’ huge trade for Jeffery Simmons, who has more tackles for loss since 2021 than any other defensive tackle in the NFL, will immediately help the run defense, and his ability to collapse the pocket will immediately help Chicago’s pass rush. I could see him on a limited snap count since he won’t know the calls, twists, and stunts, but he’ll play in some obvious passing or running situations. But JSN will still be a problem. Smith-Njigba, the 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year, is having an even better 2026, averaging 8.3 receptions and 123.9 receiving yards per game. He’s the type of game-altering talent who can win a game on his own. So far, Chicago’s defense has played better than many expected, but I don’t know how they’ll limit JSN. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have his over/under on receptions at 7.5 and receiving yards at 99.5, and while those are high — relatively speaking — they seem easily attainable for him vs. Chicago’s secondary. The Bears don’t have a corner on the roster who can hang with him. But to be fair, neither do most teams. I like the over on both of those. My guess is the Bears will be focused on stopping the run, knowing JSN will get his, while trying to heat up Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold into making mistakes. And now with a game-wrecking defensive tackle in Simmons, the Bears won’t need to blitz as much, so they’ll be able to keep a safety over the top of JSN a few more times. Another over I like is Caleb Williams’ rushing yards, which is at 21.5. This will be his third game back after the hamstring injury, and the extra rest following their Thursday nighter should have his legs feeling good enough to take off when the opportunity presents itself. item.title: Arizona men’s tennis: Clancy Shields committed for the long haul after breakthrough season
item.description: For the better part of a decade, Arizona men’s tennis was knocking on the door of college tennis’ version of the promised land, the NCAA Championships. This spring, Clancy Shields ’ program broke through by advancing to the NCAA quarterfinals for the first time in history. The achievement affirmed Arizona’s status as one of the sport’s rising programs. The experience also affirmed Shields’ desire to stay in Tucson and build out a program he thinks can compete with anyone nationally. Shields, who is entering his 11th year as Arizona’s head coach, signed a contract in August that runs through the 2030-31 season. The announcement may have gone under the radar, but it was one of the biggest moves athletic director Desiree Reed-Francois made during the offseason. Not that Reed-Francois needed to do a lot of selling. “I told Desiree, ‘I want always to be — if I can and if you guys are willing to do it — I want to have a contract that the players who end up coming here feel like I’m going to be here and that there’s stability,’” Shields said last month. “If you come to play for Arizona you’re going to come play for me for the entirety of your career.” Shields’ decision to staying in one place comes off as refreshing in an era where coaches and players are all too often willing to jump at the highest-paying suitor, even when they’ve got a good thing going where they are. Shields has no doubt had chances to look elsewhere after taking over a program with a lackluster history and turning it into one of the best programs in the Western states. Shields’ program is coming off a fifth consecutive conference championship. The Wildcats concluded 2026 with a No. 7 ranking, the highest final ranking in program history. And for the second year in a row, Arizona produced an All-American standout — first Colton Smith followed by Jay Friend . “The grass isn’t always greener somewhere else,” Shields said. “As much as people will try to come poach you or say ‘Hey, come to this place, you can do things here,’ I always say that with (players), If you’re looking to get in the portal or doing this, we’ve all had the opportunity to look around and do things. “This is what makes this place special is that we’ve all committed to being here and to grow this place, to grow this program and the culture that we’ve built.” Shields’ philosophy defies the transactional culture that defines much of college athletics. He applies it to his recruiting strategy, opting for players who he believes want to come to Arizona for the school as much as the chance to chase titles. “We talk to recruits and say, ‘Look, this isn’t a mercenary thing where we hire somebody and try to pay them a bunch of money and hope they win a bunch of matches for us,’” Shields said. “This is a developmental program where we bring you in, you go through your time here, and by the time you leave, you’ve got the tools to go out and make a deep run and play professionally.” The message gets through to the team, as evid

item.title: Weekend Warm-up: Halloween 2026 — Bayern Munich players as movie villains; A Spooky Mix of Halloween Songs; Bundesliga predictions; and MORE!
item.description: (Photo by Charles-McClintock Wilson/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Forget Halloween. Forget haunted houses. Forget whatever nightmare factory Hollywood is cooking up next. If Bayern Munich players were horror movie villain s, the Bundesliga would need a support group, a priest, and probably a few extra goalkeepers. Let’s just say that fac ing this Bayern Munich squad would be less like playing a football match and more like starring in a horror franchise where nobody makes it to the sequel. Harry Kane — Jason Voorhees (Friday the 13th) He floats into the final third, smiles at his helpless victims, and then proceeds to make their next 90 minutes a living nightmare. His vision is disturbingly good, his passing is frightening, and his ability to make defenders disappear is downright supernatural. You’ll see him in your dreams. Michael Olise — Pennywise (IT) He floats into the final third, smiles at his helpless victims, and then proceeds to make their next 90 minutes a living nightmare. His vision is disturbingly good, his passing is frightening, and his ability to make defenders disappear is downright supernatural. You’ll see him in your nightmares. Manuel Neuer — Michael Myers (Halloween) The original boogeyman. You think you’ve finally beaten him, you think you’ve found an opening, and then somehow he’s standing right in front of you again. Neuer has been terrifying strikers for so long that some of them have probably retired simply to avoid seeing him in the penalty area. Jamal Musiala — Freddy Krueger (A Nightmare on Elm Street) His ability to dribble through defenders is practically dreamlike. Opponents go to sleep thinking they’ve figured him out, only to wake up screaming after he’s danced through their entire defense. You can’t escape Musiala by closing your eyes. That’s when he does his best work. Dayot Upamecano — Leatherface (The Texas Chain Saw Massacre) An absolute physical nightmare. When Upa is in full flight, opposing attackers hear the chainsaw, look over their shoulders, and realize they have approximately 0.3 seconds to make a decision. Sometimes he catches you. Sometimes he catches absolutely everything. Jonathan Tah — Pinhead (Hellraiser) You thought you were entering a football match. Congratulations, you’ve entered another dimension of suffering. Tah is big, imposing, and not particularly interested in making life comfortable for opposing forwards. Welcome to the pain box. Joshua Kimmich — Jigsaw (Saw) He doesn’t necessarily need to tackle you. He’ll simply give you a tactical puzzle with 14 possible solutions, none of which you can figure out before he steals the ball. The game is simple: survive 90 minutes against Kimmich’s pressing traps. Most participants fail. Luis Díaz — Chucky (Child’s Play) Terrifying, relentless, and absolutely capable of ruining your afternoon. You think you’ve dealt with him, only to discover he’s somehow back, running at you again. item.title: Angels Lose Promising Utility Man on Waivers to Open Offseason
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The New York Mets claimed Los Angeles Angels infielder Kyren Paris off of waivers Thursday, ending his seven-year stint in the organization. The Angels drafted Paris in the second round of the 2019 draft, and he featured in parts of four seasons for the team in MLB. INF Kyren Paris has been claimed off waivers by the New York Mets — Angels PR (@LAAngelsPR) October 29, 2026 Paris played in eight hames for the Angels in 2026, striking out eight times in 15 hitless at-bats while walking three times. He saw his longest run of MLB action in 2025, when he had. blistering start to the season after breaking camp with the team. Paris had an OPS higher than 1.000 through the middle of April in 2025 before falling into a slump and returning to Triple-A. Through his 88 games in MLB from 2023-26, Paris had seven homers and 17 RBIs, posting a .510 OPS with 101 strikeouts in 232 at-bats. Paris featured in both Double-A and Triple-A this season, posting a .842 OPS in 93 games, though he had a .981 OPS in Triple-A. The Angels didn’t have an explicit need for Paris in their team, as their outfield consisted of players better than him for the majority of the season. Mike Trout obviously commanded a spot in the outfield for the entire season, and Wade Meckler also made himself at home with some strong performances throughout the year. Factoring in Christian Moore’s transition to outfield and the contributions of players like Jose Siri, Josh Lowe and Bryce Teodosio, there wasn’t much room for Paris. Feb 24, 2026; Tempe, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Angels infielder Kyren Paris (19) trots back to the dugout after the second inning against the San Francisco Giants during a spring training game at Tempe Diablo Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Allan Henry-Imagn Images Who Else Did the Angels Put on Waivers? Paris wasn’t the only player the Angels placed on waivers to start the offseason, but he is the sole player to depart thus far. Left-handed Pitcher Sammy Peralta and catcher Sebastián Rivero both landed on waivers, though they both cleared them before the organization sent them outright to Triple-A. The Angels now have three more open roster spots, allowing them to be a little more active in the offseason as they look to bounce back from the first 100-loss season in Franchise history. Before that, though, they have to sort out their vacant managerial position and find a replacement for interim general manager John Mozeliak, who filled in for the team after they fired Perry Minasian. The post Angels Lose Promising Utility Man on Waivers to Open Offseason appeared first on LA Sports Report .

item.title: Newcastle Joins Premier League Rivals in Chase of FC Twente Teenager
item.description: ENSCHEDE - Ruud Nijstad of FC Twente walks onto the pitch ahead of the UEFA Conference League match between FC Twente and FC Thun at De Grolsch Veste on October 15, 2026 in Enschede, the Netherlands. WART BRINKERHOF / ANP (Photo by ANP via Getty Images) | ANP via Getty Images Newcastle United continues to monitor young defensive talents across Europe, with another teenage center-back now emerging on the club’s radar ahead of 2027. According to TEAMtalk’s Graeme Bailey , Newcastle is among several Premier League clubs tracking FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad, alongside Manchester United, Manchester City, Brentford, Aston Villa, Everton and Sunderland. “Sources have confirmed to TEAMtalk that Manchester City, Brentford, Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Everton and Sunderland have all checked on Nijstad this season,” Bailey reported. The 18-year-old stands 6-foot-5, is left-footed and made his first-team breakthrough at Twente last season. Newcastle’s interest remains at a scouting stage for now, with no indication that an offer or negotiations have taken place already. Bailey reported that Twente expects interest in Nijstad to intensify during 2027, but the club has no intention of allowing him to leave during the January window. “Sources indicate that Twente are anticipating Nijstad’s growing list of admirers could intensify their interest during 2027,” Bailey wrote. “However, the Dutch club are not looking to sanction a deal in the January transfer window.” Nijstad has a market value estimated at €18 million, according to Transfermarkt. For Newcastle, being linked to the youngster fits the club’s broader effort to identify high-upside defenders early rather than wait until they become established senior players, although competition for his services could prove tough to overcome. Would Nijstad be the type of young center-back Newcastle should move for in 2027, or should the Magpies go for another under-the-radar gem? Share your thoughts in the comments. Join the conversation! item.title: WNBA fans react to Angel Reese snapping at a Valkyries player during Game 6 win
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Angel Reese had another brilliant performance in the WNBA Finals to help the Atlanta Dream to secure a dominant 80-69 win against the Golden State Valkyries. The Bayou Barbie finished the game with 15 points and 14 boards, while also contributing a steal and a block. She struggled shooting the ball, but ensured her contributions off the ball helped the team get over the line. In a game that was heavily debated due to the early start time, Reese made sure to bring in all the energy right from the tip-off. The crowd played a factor as the Dream started the game on top, taking a 17-point lead after the first quarter itself. This was extended to 20 points at halftime and although the Valkyries tried to fight back in the second half, the Dream had done enough to force a Game 7. Fans react to Angel Reese’s interaction with the Golden State Valkyries bench Reese continued her antics with the players on the Valkyries, as she was seen getting into it with their bench players. This further hyped up the crowd, who were cheering on the Dream. This was not the first time Reese tried to take on a Valkyries player. Earlier in the series, she was seen trash-talking Aminata Gueye. She has also had complaints about the referees during the series, which have led to heated press conferences. Fans were quick to react when a video of Reese trash-talking to the Valkyries bench went viral. “I don’t know if I could dislike her more,” said one fan. While another added: “Now if they lose game 7 she’s gonna go on a she’s the victim campaign.” Someone also wrote: “Just imagine what a championship will do to that p****.” A fan opined: “You’d think she can make layups with the way she talks.” “Angel only talks when she’s up, when she’s down it’s crickets. (Or complaining)” said a fan. Reese will be hoping that she can put up another big performance in the all-important Game 7, which will be played at the Ballhalla on October 31. item.title: Syracuse Football: Opponent Q and A’s with Steve Helwick
item.description: DALLAS, TX - SEPTEMBER 26: SMU Mustangs head coach Rhett Lashlee looks on during warm-ups during the college football game between the SMU Mustangs and the Missouri State Bears on September 26, 2025, at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After last week’s thrilling win against North Carolina, Syracuse football turns its attention to 19th ranked SMU on Saturday. With that, comes everyone’s favorite Opponent Q and A’s. A huge thanks to Steve Helwick from Underdog Dynasty on SB Nation joining us again this year to talk Mustangs. TNIAAM: During the last three weeks SMU has played down to competition in the ACC. How can the Orange take advantage? SH: Inopportune turnovers, penalties, and a shaky kicking game. SMU essentially lost the turnover battle 4-0 against Florida State (was actually 4-1 because FSU fumbled on its last-ditch lateral play) and 3-0 against Louisville. Then against Missouri State, the Mustangs committed 12 penalties and lost the turnover battle 2-1. Take those mistakes out of the equation, and SMU’s offense has moved the ball exceptionally well — Boston College game aside — ranking 13th nationally in yards per game and first downs. Meanwhile, the defense has been fairly consistent every week except the Louisville game when it allowed countless explosive runs. Only Louisville has scored more than 24 on the Mustangs this season. All of SMU’s issues were suddenly fixed in the second half of last week’s Cal game, where the Mustangs finally lived up to their potential with a 42-0 second half surge. Syracuse has been turnover prone this year, particularly in the passing game. For the Orange, limiting those interceptions and winning this turnover battle is a must against a balanced SMU offense which moves well through a variety of skill position players. Also, Syracuse has improved against the run in the past few weeks. Stifling Kendrick Raphael should be the priority, as SMU’s offense saw its greatest struggles when Boston College loaded the box and contained the run game in the Week 5 matchup. TNIAAM: Kevin Jennings is on pace for his best season in Dallas, what has Jennings improved on since the Orange saw him last year? SH: For starters, I’d say his health. Kevin Jennings doesn’t get enough credit for how he fought through nearly the entire 2025 season on an ankle injury. The injury evidently affected his rushing numbers, as he declined from 354 yards in 2024 to 54 in 2025. This year, Jennings is significantly more mobile and has 121 rushing yards and two touchdowns, equipped with the ability to extend more plays moving about the pocket. Also, his accuracy has taken a significant forward. Jennings is completing 72.6 percent of passes (fifth among FBS quarterbacks with 100 attempts), which is especially impressive given the depth of many of his throws. He has yet to finish a game under 63 percent accuracy, and he has also notably limited h

item.title: Roma make first approach for Frosinone’s Kvernadze
item.description: Roma make first approach for Frosinone’s Kvernadze Massimiliano Alvini’s Frosinone never ceases to amaze, and they’re the great revelation of this Serie A season. The Gialloblu crushed Lecce 5-1 yesterday and continue to occupy the top spots of the table. One of the players who stood out the most is undoubtedly Giorgi Kvernadze. The Georgian attacking winger also managed to make an impact against Lecce, recording two assists in an excellent performance. In recent weeks, interest has been shown from Roma, who are seeking significant reinforcements in that area of ​​the pitch. Gian Piero Gasperini is looking for attacking wingers with certain characteristics, and the 2003-born player’s profile is a particular favorite at Trigoria. As Nicolò Schira reported, Roma is among the clubs that have already approached Kvernadze. Competition, however, is already stiff: Crystal Palace, Monaco, and Everton, owned by the Friedkins, have also expressed their interest.

item.title: Cowboys have chance they can’t let fly away against Cardinals
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images Halloween weekend is fast approaching, and for a Dallas Cowboys team desperate to stack wins for the first time this season, there may be no spookier, scarier sight than the Arizona Cardinals coming to town. Yeah, seriously. Even within a bad NFC East division, the Cowboys have created a small margin of error to lose games they’re supposed to win, having already dropped such games to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Giants. The Cowboys suffered their fifth loss of the 2025 season to the Cardinals in week nine at home last year, and now are looking to avoid the same amount of losses through week seven against the same opponent – one they haven’t beaten since 2017, even with three of the four meetings since that win in Arizona coming in Arlington. If not for that 28-17 Cowboys win in 2017, the Cardinals would actually have an active nine-game winning streak against the Cowboys coming into this weekend, with the last win before that one coming in 2006. The 2-5 Cardinals opened their season with what felt like an upset win at the time at the Chargers, who remain winless. In week six, they went back to SoFi Stadium and scored a legitimate upset against a division rival, beating the Rams 18-16. This snapped a four-game losing streak to the Seahawks, 49ers, Giants, and Lions, but Mike LaFleur’s team also could not stack wins as they lost last Sunday at home to the Broncos. Let’s get to our weekly look at what the Cowboys must do to finally get the monkey cardinal off their back and beat these pesky red birds, or what could throw the season back off the rails with another bad home loss. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Arizona Cardinals if… …they set the edge on defense. There was one thing the Cowboys still struggled to do for the majority of the Philadelphia Eagles game. While the offense got points early and kept the pressure on most of the night, and the defense avoided the backbreaking plays and penalties until that offense handed them a sizeable lead, and the kicking game swung the field position battle in Dallas’ favor, still, the defense had a hard time setting the edge. If ever the stage was set for a game to help prove the Cowboys are different this year, Sunday afternoon is the ultimate “do-over” game, because the defense couldn’t set an edge at all against Jacoby Brissett and these Cardinals under Matt Eberflus in 2025. A strong run game on the edge, missed tackles, and the dual-threat ability of Brissett also gave the Cowboys defense no chance to hold up in coverage, as Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride caught touchdowns – the latter making the score 24-7 in the third quarter. Christian Parker’s Cowboys defense showed new looks in the middle of the field against the Eagles with Shemar James and Demarvion Overshown at linebacker. The personnel elsewhere in the secondary is also better than when these teams met last season when Markquese Bell, Juanyeh Thomas, and Kaiir Elam all started.

item.title: Indiana men’s basketball 2026-27 player preview: Darren Harris
item.description: Indiana Hoosiers guard Darren Harris (1) celebrates a three-point basket Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, during a preseason game at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. The Indiana Hoosiers defeated the Butler Bulldogs, 96-68. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Every good basketball team needs at least one reliable 3-point shooter, the kind of guy who can draw defenses out to the perimeter and open up space in the middle. Indiana had that last year in Lamar Wilkerson, who was one of the more prolific deep threats in the country in his lone season in Bloomington. He joined the program with plenty of proven production at the mid-major level, so there was an expectation for him to take on that role. The Hoosiers don’t have that kind of proven college experience this year. Instead, the staff is leaning on former Duke transfer Darren Harris to make good on the promise he showed in high school. G Darren Harris Position: Wing Year: Third Role: Starting shooting guard/3-point specialist Previous school: Duke Harris comes to Bloomington after having spent the first two seasons of his career with Duke, playing sparse minutes off the bench for two extraordinarily talented Blue Devils rosters. He was rated as a 4-star prospect in the class of 2024 by the 247Sports composite, being listed as a small forward with a height of 6’6”. He had a remarkably strong reputation as a 3-point shooter in high school, both for his ability to make shots from deep and his quickness in releasing the ball. He’s able to shoot on the move, but doesn’t do too much off the dribble. Now, with Darian DeVries giving him the ultimate green light at Indiana, he’ll have an opportunity to show his shooting prowess. The challenge for Harris is twofold at Indiana. He’s gotta prove he really can shoot the ball well at this level and he’s more veratile beyond that. Harris hasn’t done much aside from shoot during his brief minutes at Duke and the run he’s gotten in exhibition play at Indiana. He hasn’t been close enough to the rim to be on hand for rebounds, but he’s got great size for the backcourt to be able to get after the ball. He also hasn’t shown too much as a driver, which is interesting given you’d think his shot form would allow him to convert well from the free throw line. He also has to find passing opportunities. If he shoots well and gets defended as such, he should find ways to pass out of it in such a way that sets the Hoosiers up for some easy scores. DeVries has spoken of Harris’ shooting ability with great faith. That’s what any good coach would do, and he’s gonna try to keep Harris confident, but Indiana’s going to need its go-to 3-point shooting option to, well, do that well. Join the conversation! item.title: A Camden Chat Thanks, and Farewell
item.description: Dear Camden Chatters, today is my last day as a writer for this blog. I’ve been writing here since the 2019 season, though I was a fan way before that. I definitely won’t stop being a fan of this site, but I’m hanging up my cleats as a writer today. I want to say thanks. Back in 2014, when Adam Jones circled Oriole Park carrying the AL East Champions flag after the team clinched, then pied a bunch of people in the face, I felt a real urge to share the joy somewhere. Same, too, with the Delmon Young double—could you believe how noisy the stadium was? Same, a few years later, when John Means pitched a no-hitter. And when the O’s won the division title in 2023 and Gunnar Henderson was named Rookie of the Year. And many others. Those moments are special because you have people to share them with, like this community. I loved being a part of it as a writer. Now, I won’t deny that I wasn’t always a good writer. There have been some very bad takes on my part in seven years. I thought utility superman Stevie Wilkerson should get regular playing time. I believed in the Shintaro Fujinami reclamation project . I got on the Spenser Watkins bandwagon, if such a thing even existed. There were times it was hard to write, because the on-field product sucked. I did a whole piece on whether the 2021 Orioles, who finished 52-110, were the worst O’s team in history. (They have a strong claim. Maikel Franco played a bunch, we tried to fix Matt Harvey, and Pat Valaika was an infield fixture. Blech.) The team never did win a single playoff game while I was a writer here. I’ve been frustrated by some of the recent changes I’ve seen. I hope the term “ liftoff ” is soon forgotten, because if it’s remembered, I think it will be ironically, meaning the Orioles will continue to be bad. I wish Heston Kjerstad had panned out. I wish the team hadn’t traded Trey Mancini, or Ramón Urías, and especially not Adley Rutschman this year, I don’t care what the return was. Brandon Hyde getting fired in May 2025 felt like a real admission of internal chaos, and so many internal changes this offseason suggest this remains true. But even so, it’s always made me happy to write about baseball. In my day job, I teach law and write long articles with 400 footnotes. Do people enjoy reading them? I hope someone does, but writing about baseball is another thing altogether. I love telling a good story, and baseball is full of them. In seven seasons, I got to recap some great moments. There was a 6-3 win on Camden Yards’ 30th anniversary , a day that saw Brooks Robinson, Mike Mussina and Eddie Murray all come back to town. More recently, I wrote about Colton Cowser’s ridiculous home-run robbing catch , maybe the best thing I’ve seen him do in his whole career. I got to pay homage to backup catcher James McCann getting hit in the nose with a fastball, then staying in the game. I recapped Kyle Bradish’s first start back from Tommy John surgery and his MLB debut years before. Speaking of debuts, Gunna

item.title: Texas vs. Mississippi State: How to watch, date, time, TV channel
item.description: Texas finishes a stretch of three straight home games against a Mississippi State team without its starting quarterback. (Ricardo B. Brazziell/American-Statesman) A stretch of three straight home games ends for Texas this weekend against Mississippi's other SEC team. After a wild win over then-No. 7 Ole Miss last week, the No. 11 Longhorns (5-2, 2-2 SEC) host Mississippi State on Saturday night. The Bulldogs (4-3, 2-3) will be without dynamic quarterback Kamario Taylor, who's out for the season with a toe injury. Texas leads the all-time series 4-2, including two wins as SEC opponents. Last year's game in Starkville, Miss., was a wild affair that saw the Longhorns erase a 38-21 deficit with less than 10 minutes left, tying the score on Eisenhower graduate Ryan Niblett's 79-yard punt return for a touchdown with 1:47 left. In overtime, backup QB Matthew Caldwell threw a 10-yard TD pass to Emmett Mosley V for a 45-38 win. Texas vs. Mississippi State When: 6:30 p.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium, Austin TV: ABC with Joe Tessitore (play-by-play), Jesse Palmer (analyst) and Kris Budden (sideline reporter); also streaming on Disney+. item.title: Injured Tuipulotu a doubt for England's autumn Tests
item.description: Kepu Tuipulotu joined Bath in 2024 [Getty Images] Hooker Kepu Tuipulotu has emerged as a doubt for England's Nations Championship campaign after picking up a knee injury in national training on Tuesday. The uncapped 21-year-old had been tipped to make his England breakthrough this autumn. However, it is understood he will not be included in the England squad for the opener with Australia on 8 November, with an exact timeframe on his return unclear. Tuipulotu also qualifies for Wales, the country of his birth, and was even invited to train with the senior side by then-coach Warren Gatland but opted to focus on England. He joined Bath's academy in 2024 and signed a contract with the club until 2028 earlier this year. Scrum-half Archie McParland is also an injury concern, and has not been included in the Northampton squad to face Gloucester at the weekend, while fly-half Fin Smith is a major doubt for the Wallabies fixture. In more positive injury news, Gloucester Seb Atkinson has been named at inside centre for the Cherry and Whites as he bids to prove his fitness. England also face Japan and New Zealand next month, before the Nations Championship finals weekend at the end of November. item.title: Pitcher Chooses Free Agency Over Brewers Return After Winning World Series
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May Dustin May was traded from the St. Louis Cardinals to the Milwaukee Brewers this season, but now he will be looking for a new contract. According to the New York Post's Jon Heyman , May has declined his $20 million mutual option. If May did not decline his half, the Brewers surely would have declined theirs. While May had some great moments with the team, he was not worth $20 million. The Brewers typically don't spend that money on anyone, let alone a starting pitcher who was inconsistent for them. May did have three quality starts for the Brewers and pitched in five games during their World Series run. In the Fall Classic, he made two appearances, allowing two earned runs across four innings of work. His declining his option is something the Brewers likely foresaw when they traded for him. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! He now has four rings, despite only playing in the postseason three times. He got rings for his efforts on the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2024 and 2025 despite missing all of 2024 and not pitching in the 2025 postseason. He did play a meaningful role for the Brewers this season, and could return on a cheaper, short-term deal if no other team wants to sign him. There were moments when he looked like a potential difference-maker for the Brewers, and perhaps a full offseason of work with the team could help him. However, plenty of other teams could be willing to take a shot on him and give him a real shot at a rotation spot. On the Brewers, he would need to steal a spot from either Quinn Priester or Kyle Harrison. More MLB: Bo Bichette Reportedly Returning To Mets On $42 Million Option

item.title: Former Celtic defender handed career lifeline with unexpected transfer
item.description: Former Celtic defender handed career lifeline with unexpected transfer Former Celtic defender Shane Duffy has secured a return to football after signing a short-term deal with Championship side Derby County. The 34-year-old has been without a club since leaving Norwich City in the summer, having last made a competitive appearance in November 2025. Duffy, who spent the 2020/21 campaign on loan at Celtic from Brighton, made 27 appearances during a difficult season at Parkhead before returning south. The Republic of Ireland international subsequently joined Fulham before moving to Norwich in 2023, but has now been handed an opportunity to revive his career at Pride Park. After impressing during a trial period, Duffy has signed an initial two-month contract as Derby look to address a growing list of defensive injuries. A club statement confirmed: “Derby County have completed the signing of Shane Duffy on a short-term deal. The 34-year-old has penned an initial two-month contract in DE24 following a trial period with the club. “Duffy adds extensive experience to the Rams’ defensive ranks, with the towering centre-back nearing 500 professional appearances across club and international football. At international level, Duffy has represented the Republic of Ireland 61 times – scoring seven goals – since his debut in 2014. “The Irishman will be in available on Saturday when the Rams travel to Millwall (3pm kick-off).” HAVE YOUR SAY – Join the Celtic conversation in our comments section below… Celtic in the Fifties by Matt Corr, in two volumes, both published on 4th September 2026 by Celtic Star Books. item.title: Jorge Posada was right about Yankees — and that’s not even the worst of it | Klapisch
item.description: The Yankees are saying goodbye to the worst month in franchise history, and it goes far beyond the shellacking they took from the Rays in the AL Division Series. It’s what’s happened since that says the Yankees are due for a major overhaul. Here’s what the public relations disaster looks like to date: *Franchise legends Derek Jeter , Paul O’Neill, CC Sabathia and Alex Rodriguez have all savaged the clubhouse culture. *Owner Hal Steinbrenner took no responsibility for the latest October failure. *Manager Aaron Boone , who has yet to win a championship in his nine years on the job, said, “I believe we can win with me at the helm. … I think I’m good at my job.” * Jorge Posada , a beloved member of the Core Four, believes he’s no longer welcome at spring training . *Brewers manager Pat Murphy, celebrating the franchise’s first world championship on Wednesday, called the Yankees “horses---” and accused them of “playing for [themselves].” If none of this embarrasses Steinbrenner, then he might as well go into hiding forever. The pointless once-a-year press conferences do nothing but enrage the fan base anyway. My advice to Steinbrenner is to take the final step and stay away entirely. But before Steinbrenner vanishes, he should take a closer look at the two most damaging indictments against the Yankees. Steinbrenner can start by asking why an esteemed champion like Posada believes he’s being snubbed. Second, Steinbrenner should demand to know how the Yankees have fallen so far that a small-market manager like Murphy is comfortable trashing his team, moments after winning the World Series. Are the Yankees that much of an industry joke? Have the people in charge allowed North America’s most iconic franchise to turn into the MLB’s laughingstock? It wasn’t that long ago that the Yankees were the industry’s most prestigious club. As O’Neill told me earlier this month , “You’re the New York Yankees. You’re different because of the tradition and because of the name: New York Yankees .” That history should still mean something — certainly to the current generation. That’s why Posada’s accusation, which he made during a New York Post podcast, was so shocking. I don’t believe Posada was referring to the front office or to Boone, who personally invites former Yankees to spring training. The franchise itself has made sure to honor Posada over the years. They’ve retired his No. 20, awarded him a plaque in Monument Park in 2015 and invited him to the 25 th anniversary ceremony for the 1998 team in 2023 and the Sept. 11 memorial event at Yankee Stadium last month. I reached out to two former Yankees on Thursday, neither of whom wanted to discuss Posada’s comments on the record. They consider the matter between the former catcher and the team’s hierarchy, pointing out that a number of retired stars, including Tino Martinez, Bernie Williams and Ron Guidry, come to spring training every year. “If the older guys were a problem, then why are guys like Gator and Tino alway

item.title: Ben Davies considering move to coaching or boardroom post-retirement
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 19: Ben Davies of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates after scoring their third goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Coventry City at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 19, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Sebastian Frej/MB Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ben Davies isn’t planning on retiring anytime soon, but he’s already starting to think about what comes next in his career. A fan favorite and currently the longest-tenured player at Tottenham Hotspur, Davies is beloved at Spurs and deeply respected by the club and every manager that has come and gone over the last decade when he’s been at the club. But Davies is 33 now, the Wales national team captain, and understands that all things must come to an end eventually. In an interview with the BBC, Davies says that while he hopes to keep playing football for a few more years, he’s looking at what happens after he hangs up his boots — and that he’d be interested in both a coaching role, or even a move to the boardroom of a football club. “Look, hopefully [retirement] is still quite a few years away. I feel fit. I love playing football, and I want to play as long as I can. But you’re a long time retired in this game, and I don’t see myself just doing nothing after football. “For me, it’s a great learning experience as well – to see how it all works behind the scenes in the world of football. This is a great start. It’s more than just a role for me; it’s great to be able to give back as much as I can to a footballing country that’s given me so much. “It’s hard to put a nail in it where your future lies. If something falls on my lap in the coaching world, then maybe that will be my route. But I want to be able to use my expertise and what I’ve learned in the best way that it can be, and I don’t know what angle that takes after football yet. “I’d like to be someone who maybe, at some point, crosses that divide from a player to the boardroom or a front-office kind of role, because I haven’t seen too many players over the years who have done that. “I think it definitely adds a pretty good perspective when making decisions.” I think we all expected Davies to move into coaching after his playing days are done. He has completed his UEFA A License already, which means he’s already qualified to lead U18 teams, be a top assistant coach, or even manage a Championship club. (He would need his UEFA Pro License in order to manage a top-level club in European football.) It wouldn’t shock me if he would immediately move to Tottenham’s coaching ranks, or possibly a coaching position in Wales, after calling it quits on his playing days. Davis is also a super smart guy and I find it fascinating that he’d consider a boardroom role as well. item.title: The Daily: Red Wings Players ‘Happy With Guys Who are Here’; Edvinsson Update
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With Dylan Larkin saying he doesn’t want to spend any more time with the Detroit Red Wings, his former teammates are ready to move on without him. “It’s his decision,” Alex DeBrincat said after the Red Wings downed Chicago 4-1. “We’re happy with the guys who are here and we’re confident in our group here. So we’re ready to move forward and keep getting wins.” Despite a summer of turmoil that include Larkin’s trade request and Simon Edvinsson remaining unsigned, the Red Wings are 5-1-3 in their last nine games. They are one point out of a playoff spot. “I think we want this to be a proud organization,” DeBrincat added, “and we want players to be here and want to be here long-term.” Overcoming months of adversity has become a rallying cry for this group. The Red Wings’ next game is Saturday against the St. Louis Blues. In Case You Missed It Coach Todd McLellan says the Red Wings are developing a new identity. Former captain Dylan Larkin i s giving up plenty of dollars by deciding to leave the Red Wings Red Wings Extra Horcoff answered a multitude of questions about Dylan Larkin and the only one asked about Edvinsson. item.title: North Korean group blamed for $6.3bn Binance hack in biggest ever crypto heist
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange scrambles to freeze affected assets, with about $3bn located so far, and says it will cover losses Tell us: have you been affected by the Binance hack? item.title: ‘I was warned not to buy car or house’ — Nigerian Pastor recounts ritual wealth
item.description: Pastor Joel Olasunkanmi, an Ogbomoso based cleric, has recounted how his pursuit of wealth through ritual practices allegedly led to a life changing car accident that resulted in the amputation of his leg. Olasunkanmi shared his experience during an interview with BBC Yoruba, saying he turned to a ritualist while pursuing what he described as vain and worldly things. According to the pastor, his involvement in the practice lasted about five years, during which he was instructed to find a young woman he deeply loved and carry out a ritual involving her. “Thirty years ago, I took some steps that made God angry. It was while I was searching for vain and worldly things that I became disabled. I had a car accident on May 26, 2001,” he said. Recounting the instructions given to him by the ritualist, Olasunkanmi alleged that he was asked to find a woman he loved, have sexual intercourse with her and use a white handkerchief to wipe her private parts before presenting it to the ritualist. “The ritualist I sought told me to look for a young lady that I so much loved. I searched for her, had sex with her and used a white handkerchief to wipe her genitals. I took it to the man,” he recounted. He said the ritual eventually brought him wealth, although he claimed he did not fully understand how it happened. However, he alleged that the ritualist placed restrictions on how he could spend the money. “I did become rich. I did not know how it happened. But I did become rich. But I was told I could not buy a car or house from it,” he said. The pastor further disclosed that the vehicle involved in the accident that eventually led to the amputation of his leg was indirectly connected to him because he had provided the money used to purchase it for another person. “At the end of the day, the car that hit me was indirectly mine because I was the one who bought it for him. At the end of the day, my leg was amputated,” he said. Reflecting on his experience, Olasunkanmi urged young Nigerians to exercise patience and avoid seeking quick wealth through questionable means. “I implore the youths of today to be patient in everything they do,” he advised.
