item.title: How did the biggest crypto heist in history just happen?
item.description: Binance is the biggest cryptocurrency exchange ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange Binance has been hit with the biggest ever cryptocurrency heist, in which billions of dollars of reserves were drained in just 20 minutes. From 8:05pm on 29 October, $6.36 billion in cryptocurrencies were shifted from wallets in a coordinated attack believed to have originated from a North Korean-linked hacking unit called TraderTraitor. This group was also behind a $1.5 billion hack of the Bybit crypto exchange in February 2025. The US Treasury has previously said that such stolen funds are used to finance North Korea’s nuclear missile programme. Advertisement Despite cryptocurrency’s founding idea of decentralisation, meaning no one has singular control over the money flowing through the network, there are some large single points of failure. It is thought one of these was the cause of the Binance hack, which gave access to a system the exchange uses to authorise transfers out of customers’ accounts. Read more Quantum computer quickly mines cryptocurrency while using less energy In a statement , Binance said its early investigations indicate the security incident may stem from a compromised laptop belonging to an engineer. TRM Labs, a cybersecurity firm, suggests that preparations for the attack may have begun several days ago. The company claims it has found no evidence that the private cryptographic keys used to authorise transactions were stolen. Instead, the attackers appear to have gained access to the software that requests withdrawals, potentially allowing them to instruct Binance’s own systems to approve the transfers. However, the investigation is continuing and the firm has said in a subsequent statement there may have been “additional points of breach”. “It shouldn’t be possible for a single [developer] PC to be compromised and somehow for that to allow the entire exchange to be compromised,” says Alan Woodward at the University of Surrey, UK. “I don’t understand how that can happen unless they’ve got the most ridiculous operational security.” If that is the case, it highlights how precarious major financial hubs in the crypto world can be to single points of failure. Free newsletter Sign up to The Weekly Sign up to newsletter “You can build a vault with mathematical firewalls, but if the individual holding the keys can be duped, the vault is opened,” says Clive Summerfield at FARx, a cybersecurity company. “Most crypto platforms are as centralised as any bank, with a small number of privileged individuals controlling billions. The difference is that once crypto is transferred, it’s gone.” That centralisation can be a blessing as well as a curse, though: cryptocurrencies Tether and Circle have been able to freeze billions of dollars of stolen coins, stymying the hackers in attempts to transfer about half the stolen funds any further. item.title: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez targets early return from injury
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is targeting a return from injury earlier than expected after making progress in his recovery from a broken jaw, according to Sky Sports. The Argentina international underwent surgery after sustaining the injury during Chelsea’s visit to Everton earlier this month and had initially indicated that he would be “back in a few weeks”. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso also provided a similar recovery timeframe last week. However, Sky Sports News’ James Savundra reports that there is growing optimism that Martinez could return sooner than anticipated after consulting a specialist about having a protective mask fitted. Chelsea face Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday before travelling to Sunderland ahead of the upcoming international break. Martinez’s earlier return would be a boost for Alonso, who has relied on 21-year-old Mike Penders in the Argentine’s absence. Penders, who deputised for the former Aston Villa goalkeeper, endured a difficult outing in his first Premier League start against Tottenham last week, scoring an own goal. Martinez was immediately established as Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper following his summer move from Aston Villa. Meanwhile, Chelsea could face another defensive setback after Maxence Lacroix sustained a hamstring injury during their trip to Anfield on Wednesday. The defender was forced off before half-time, adding to Alonso’s growing injury concerns, although the Chelsea manager admitted that it was too early to determine the severity of the problem. “It’s too early to tell how serious it is,” Alonso said. “Unfortunately he felt something in his hamstring and we need a couple of days to check what the injury’s going to be.” Chelsea are already without Joao Pedro, Reece James, Martinez, Pep Chavarria and Jamie Gittens, while Moises Caicedo and Malo Gusto have also been dealing with minor fitness issues. Despite their injury problems, Morgan Rogers believes Chelsea showed character in their response to last weekend’s defeat to Tottenham, following their performance against Liverpool at Anfield. “To show that reaction shows we have players in the dressing room with character and fight – that’s all you can ask,” he said. “Of course we will get better tactically and technically in terms of the way we want to play. “We showed real fight after that loss and to put in a performance against a tough team, I’m proud of the boys and now we have to keep moving forward.” Vanguard News The post Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez targets early return from injury appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid: Drives like an EV, but there's no plug involved
item.description: Nissan provided flights from Washington, DC, to Santa Barbara, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Rogue Hybrid. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. Nissan has a new version of its best-selling Rogue SUV, and it’s launching the model here with the latest version of its e-Power hybrid system, which Ars tested back in February. Most of the hybrid cars you can buy today are parallel hybrids, which means that they have an internal combustion engine and an electric motor, both of which drive some or all of the wheels—everything works in parallel. But there’s another approach. Instead of connecting the engine to the wheels via a transmission, it can act as a generator and charge the traction battery, which in turn powers the electric motor. Since the engine and motor work in series, this is known as a series hybrid. That’s mostly how the Chevrolet Volt worked. As does Honda’s hybrid CR-V . Well, mostly; engineers worked out it was more efficient for those cars' gasoline engines to directly drive the wheels at highway speeds, something that to this day makes a certain subset of hybrid car enthusiast irrationally angry. If you know anyone like that in your life, send them to wherever the nearest Nissan dealership is, because the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is exactly what they’ve been asking for. Series hybrids Under the hood, with its crisp shut line and slim horizontal lights that give me something of a Range Rover vibe, there’s a 1.5 L, three-cylinder turbocharged direct-injection engine that generates 148 hp (110 kW). It only revs to 5,200 rpm because it’s optimized to charge the battery, not cope with the various loads of an engine connected to a gearbox and the wheels. That also allows the engine to operate at a rather impressive 42 percent thermal efficiency—we would need to look at Formula 1 engines to find higher. Read full article Comments

item.title: Watch Virgin Galactic's new 'Delta-class' space plane take to the skies for the 1st time (video)
item.description: null Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage. The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct. 28). Flying beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft, VMS Eve, Apeiron traveled from Virgin's manufacturing site in Mesa, Arizona, to its launch site, Spaceport America in New Mexico. "Seeing the ship fly beneath Eve to Spaceport America was a moment years in the making," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said in a statement on Thursday . "To our team and our astronaut community: your Spaceship has arrived." Virgin Galactic's first Delta-class space plane, named Apeiron, takes to the skies for the first time on Oct. 28, 2026, beneath the wings of its carrier plane, VMS Eve. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) Apeiron will undergo a series of checks and tests at Spaceport America, leading up to a planned start of commercial service in the spring of 2027. During those customer flights, Eve will carry Apeiron to an altitude of about 45,000 feet (13,700 meters), then drop the space plane. Apeiron will fire up its onboard rocket motor, which will carry the six-passenger, two-pilot vehicle to suborbital space. Passengers will experience a few minutes of weightlessness and get to see the curve of Earth against the blackness of space before coming down for a runway landing back at Spaceport America. Virgin Galactic has done this before, with its VSS Unity space plane. Unity flew seven commercial suborbital missions during its operational life, which ran from June 2023 to June 2024. Apeiron and other Delta-class planes are built for a much heavier workload, according to Virgin Galactic. "Designed to fly twice per week with a vehicle lifetime of more than 500 missions, each Spaceship in the next-generation fleet is built to support the economics of a scaled commercial operation, with increased flight cadence and a cost profile unprecedented in the industry," company representatives wrote in the same statement. And there will indeed be a fleet, if all goes to plan. The second Delta ship is under construction, for example, and is expected to enter service in mid-2027, according to Virgin Galactic. Apeiron and its Delta-class siblings will need to fly a lot to deal with Virgin Galactic's backlog: Nearly 700 ticket-holders are currently waiting to fly, according to the company . And demand remains high; the latest batch of seats, which were priced at $750,000 apiece, sold out. Virgin plans to sell the next tranche of tickets for $850,000 each, LATTE Luxury News reported . Another look at Apeiron. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) When Apeiron gets up and running, it will be the only game in town for suborbital space tourists. Virgin Galactic once shared the skies with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin , which flew paying customers to the final frontier on its New Shepard vehicle. New Shepard conducted 14 crewed suborbital flights between July 2021 and January 2026

item.title: China's secretive space plane is flying over the US this week — here's how to see it for yourself
item.description: null China's secretive space plane is making a series of passes over the United States in the coming days and you could spot it with your own eyes! The mysterious spacecraft, Shenlong, is currently orbiting Earth on its fourth mission . Although we don't know what it's up to, China's space agency has said it is testing technologies that "will pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space in the future." Under favorable conditions, Shenlong is bright enough to spot with the naked eye, according to Spaceweather.com . But you'll need to set your alarm early, as some of the best viewing opportunities are in the predawn sky. When and where to see China's space plane According to satellite-tracking website Heavens-Above , skywatchers across the U.S. have several opportunities to spot Shenlong between Oct. 30 and early November, weather permitting. Here are some of the most promising high-altitude passes for four major U.S. cities. All times are local, with the end of daylight saving time on Nov. 1 taken into account. Times are approximate and may change. Maximum elevation refers to the spacecraft's highest angle above the horizon, with 90° being directly overhead. Best predicted viewing opportunities City Date Local viewing window Maximum elevation New York Nov. 1 5:20-5:28 a.m. EST 78° Chicago Nov. 3 4:37-4:42 a.m. CST 85° Denver Nov. 2 5:05-5:12 a.m. MST 73° Los Angeles Nov. 2 5:42-5:51 a.m. PST 83° If clouds get in the way (or you forget to set your alarm), don't worry! There are several other opportunities over the coming days. Other promising passes City Date Local viewing window Maximum elevation New York Oct. 31 6:13–6:20 a.m. EDT 52° New York Nov. 2 5:28–5:37 a.m. EST 66° Chicago Oct. 31 6:50–6:59 a.m. CDT 74° Chicago Nov. 2 4:29–4:34 a.m. CST 64° Denver Nov. 1 4:57–5:04 a.m. MST 48° Denver Nov. 3 5:13–5:20 a.m. MST 70° Los Angeles Nov. 5 4:29–4:35 a.m. PST 69° Los Angeles Nov. 6 4:38–4:43 a.m. PST 66° How can I see Shenlong from where I live? These predictions are specific to each city, so your exact viewing times will depend on your viewing location. Shenlong pass over New York on Nov. 1 timings. The highlighted circle is the region where the satellite is at least 10° above your horizon. The size of the circle depends on the height of the satellite. (Image credit: Chris Peat/Heavens-Above) To find out when Shenlong will pass over your location, head to Heavens-Above , enter your location (in the top right corner of the page), then on the homepage look for "satellite database" under the satellites subheader. And search for "PRC TEST SPACECRAFT 4". Select "visible only" to see upcoming passes and click on a date to bring up a detailed sky chart showing the spacecraft's predicted path across the sky, including where to look and when. item.title: Review: You Can See Everything blurs the view of Elizabeth Holmes' deceit
item.description: In 2015, biomedical entrepreneur Elizabeth Holmes was Silicon Valley's golden girl, lauded as the youngest and richest self-made female billionaire thanks to the company she founded, Theranos, which was valued at $9 billion at the height of its success. Then it all came crashing down when accusations of fraud surfaced about the company's signature blood-testing device, culminating in a sensational trial. Holmes was convicted on four counts and sentenced to 11 years in prison. Holmes is back in the headlines thanks to a new film, You Can See Everything , which depicts the final days before Holmes, having exhausted her appeals , went to prison. Co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim , it's a surreal, absurdist piece that has largely been received with gushing enthusiasm and no small amount of hype, with some declaring it the best film of the year. A few contrarian voices have emerged over the past week with much-needed reality checks, but there's no denying the film is destined to be an awards-season darling. Pardon me for joining the buzzkills, but I cannot in good conscience jump on the You Can See Everything bandwagon. Sure, it has its moments, and the second half is highly entertaining, but there's nothing here to warrant all the breathless hyperbole. For all their much-touted access, Oppenheim and Fielder have produced a surprisingly shallow film that runs in circles, yielding very little fresh or novel insight—into Holmes, personally, or much else. item.title: Badenoch condemns racist attacks after ‘Nigerian scammer’ remark
item.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has condemned what she described as racist attacks against her after a former aide to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called her a “Nigerian scammer”. Badenoch accused Reform UK politicians of exploiting her Nigerian background for political advantage, insisting that attempts to use her race against her would not succeed. She spoke during an interview on ITV’s Good Morning Britain on Thursday, following a series of social media posts by Raheem Kassam, a former senior aide to Farage. Kassam, who previously served as editor-in-chief of Breitbart News, described Badenoch as an “unrelenting scammer”. In another post, he wrote, “How are people still falling for this Nigerian scammer? Don’t give her your credit card number and bank account details!” Reacting to the comments, Badenoch said, “I think it just shows the sort of people they are.” “I think they think that maybe using my race is a way for them to improve their standing. “Britain is not a racist country, and because it’s not a racist country, their racist attacks and using my race as an attack form is not going to work,” she said. The controversy also drew attention to the response of Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman, Robert Jenrick, who declined to condemn Kassam’s comments. Asked during an ITV interview whether he considered the remarks racist, Jenrick said he did not, although he acknowledged that they could be unpleasant or rude. “It’s not my place to police everybody’s tweets who may or may not be a supporter of Reform,” he said. Farage had also faced questions over whether he considered Kassam’s comments racist during an appearance on BBC Breakfast earlier in the week. “I don’t think saying somebody grew up in Nigeria is racist,” he said. Following further questioning, Farage acknowledged that the comment was excessive but maintained that it was not deliberately racist. “Do I think the comment was over the top? Yes, I do. Do I think it was intentionally racist? No, I don’t,” he added. The post Badenoch condemns racist attacks after ‘Nigerian scammer’ remark appeared first on Vanguard News .

I'm a huge fan of the name. Maybe Cowboy Space is striking while the iron is hot as the space industry frets over demand for launch outpacing supply. However, Cowboy Space lags far behind so many other launch providers nearing the launch pad with their medium-class rockets, and the company didn't have much hardware to show at this week's big reveal. In other words, don't mistake style for substance. But we're rocket fans at Ars, and we wish them luck. As always, we welcome reader submissions , and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar. Virgin's new rocket plane reaches home port . The first of Virgin Galactic's new Delta-class rocket planes left its Arizona factory Wednesday for a trip to Spaceport America in neighboring New Mexico, where it will undergo preparations for a test campaign culminating in suborbital flights to the edge of space, Ars reports . Virgin Galactic expects the craft's first commercial spaceflight to take place "early" in the second quarter of 2027, but like every other projected date in aerospace, this should be taken with a grain of salt. item.title: Accenture AI agents are sifting through applicants
item.description: Accenture is using AI across its recruiting process, although it maintains that final hiring decisions remain in human hands. Speaking to at its recent investor day, the global tech consultancy and outsourcing biz said it was using AI agents to sift through resumes (or CVs if you’re in the UK) and schedule interviews. Kate Clifford, global chief leadership and HR, said it was helping clients adopt a similar application of the nascent technology. "We call it frictionless recruiting, which is really our agentic recruiting solution. We put in an agentic recruiting solution where agents now do all the interview scheduling. Agents can screen a resume. We have assessments that deeply understand the skills of the candidates to help that process move much, much faster. Now a human always makes a hiring decision," she said. Clifford said the agent technology was used to help recruitment staff get through their work more quickly. "Our recruiters needed to spend time with candidates. They needed to spend time sourcing, but where they were actually spending their time was scheduling interviews, where they were actually spending their time was typing information into a system," she said. The executive claimed the agentic process reduced the time taken to hire for roles by 28 percent and improved candidate quality by 30 percent. AI agents also help new recruits get up to speed. Whereas it once took six months for an entry-level hire to become productive, the time has been cut to six weeks using AI agents, Clifford claimed, allowing them to produce billable work more rapidly. Accenture claims to serve around 9,000 clients — including some of the world’s largest businesses and government departments — with tech advice and services. For example, it won a contract with the US Internal Revenue Services worth $2.6 billion in 2023 . Any tech pro looking for a job with the company is likely being screened by AI as part of the process. The company also expects internal staff to get on the AI bandwagon. A memo sent to senior staff in February informed them that promotions to top roles at the corporation would necessitate "regular adoption" of AI tooling, and it is tracking usage. But not everyone is convinced by the value of AI in recruitment. A study published in 2022 found the idea that AI-powered recruitment software creates a fairer process was unfounded. A paper published in the journal Philosophy and Technology demonstrated that the software is little more than "automated pseudoscience." Tech job-hunters applying for a lucrative role at Accenture will be hoping the technology has moved on since then. ®

item.title: Tinubu prays for Nigeria’s peace, security at lesser Hajj
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described his Umrah pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia as spiritually fulfilling, saying he used the opportunity to pray for Nigeria. The president spoke with journalists shortly after performing the lesser Hajj in Makkah on Friday in an interview shared online by the Nigerian Television Authority. Asked what the spiritual exercise meant to him, particularly given his previous visit to Saudi Arabia ahead of the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu said it gave him a sense of fulfilment. “I feel good, I feel fulfilled, gives me a sense of spiritual thing for me, and the country, and the children,” he said. “I believe the love of the people, the commitment to the job, and the visible commitment to our Allah’s wish, Inshallah, and there’s no other God but Allah,” Tinubu added. The President said he prayed for peace, harmony and happiness among Nigerians, urging the need for continued faith in God. In a separate statement on Friday, his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed that Tinubu performed the Umrah early in the morning at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram. Onanuga said the president offered prayers of thanksgiving and sought Allah’s continued guidance and protection for Nigeria. He added that Tinubu prayed for national unity, lasting peace and stability, as well as an end to insecurity and other challenges confronting the country. The president also expressed optimism about Nigeria’s economic and social development, reiterating his administration’s commitment to building a peaceful and prosperous nation. item.title: Domestic droid gone amok? Don't worry, you're covered
item.description: Two insurers are teaming up to launch what every high-tech homeowner may soon need: household insurance for robotic mishaps. Humanoid robots are tipped by some to be the next big technology trend, with industry figures like Nvidia's Jensen Huang predicting they'll be everywhere from factories to the home. But as with anything AI-driven, things can go horribly wrong, especially when automatons are roaming a home carrying out tasks. They have even been labelled as potential " botnets in physical form ." The timing may be apt, then, for the UK's first domestic humanoid robot insurance policy. Specialist insurer Adrian Flux is offering to cover British customers as part of its home insurance range, underwritten by Texas-based Tokio Marine HCC. The two firms say the product is meant to get ahead of an emerging market, with domestic robots expected to appear in UK homes from 2027. Demand has already appeared in the US, where robotics and AI companies have launched humanoid robots for the home , with early models costing around $20,000. These are less like the near-human elderly care robot in the BBC comedy series Ann Droid , and more like vaguely human-shaped machines. The policy covers damage to, and theft of, the robot itself, plus any damage it causes to the home or belongings. It also includes personal liability if the android injures someone or damages their property, and emergency recovery or safe disablement of the humanoid after a sudden or unforeseen malfunction, such as - perhaps - attempting to chop off your fingers or put your cat on the stove . “As robots start to arrive in people's homes, we wanted to provide clarity on who is responsible if something goes wrong," says Gerry Bucke, general manager for the insurance biz Adrian Flux. "Like the driverless car policy we launched in 2016, it will be updated as the technology and the risks evolve." Beyond the home, investment is pouring into humanoids across a range of applications. Chinese carmaker Chery using them as showroom sales staff , while another firm has demonstrated them in automotive manufacturing . Elon Musk famously predicted thousands of Optimus robots in Tesla factories by the end of 2025, but still believes its humanoid robot will be the company’s biggest product . ®

item.title: INEC blames registration officers for AI-generated photos in voters’ register
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has blamed some of its registration officers for introducing suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other irregularities into the preliminary register of voters. INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed this on Friday during an interview on Arise Television, saying some registration officers used their login details to introduce questionable records into the commission’s database. Bayode said the irregularities were discovered through the commission’s Automated Biometric Identification System, which was deployed to examine the registration records. “We have registration officers on the field. And these registration officers, they have login details to log into the system. “So what we have found is that some of these registration officers, not all of them now, some of them across the states nationwide, they’ve done different things to bring these irregularities onto the register,” he said. He explained that while some of the photographs were generated using artificial intelligence, others were products of poor registration procedures. “Some of these pictures are AI-generated. Some of them not AI-generated, but very bad registration. And this thing got into the register by the registration officers because they have access to register people,” Bayode said. The ICT director added that the commission had identified the questionable records and established how some of the irregularities occurred, but could not determine the reasons behind the actions of the officers involved. “When the ABIS was run on the system, we saw these people. We know what they did. We know how they did it. But honestly, I don’t know why,” he added. Bayode said INEC had begun cleaning up the register before publishing its preliminary version, noting that the commission was working within the statutory 90-day period for the exercise. The disclosure comes amid public concerns over suspicious photographs and other anomalies in the preliminary register uploaded to INEC’s website on October 26. Screenshots circulated on social media had shown photographs suspected to be AI-generated attached to voter records in parts of Edo State. Other concerns included alleged duplicate entries and complaints by some registered voters that their details were missing from the online register. The post INEC blames registration officers for AI-generated photos in voters’ register appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away
item.description: 2 min read November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away NASA’s Voyager mission took advantage of a once-every-175-year alignment of the outer planets for a grand tour of the solar system. The twin spacecraft revealed details about Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune – using each planet’s gravity to send them on to the next destination. Voyager set the stage for such ambitious orbiter missions as Galileo to Jupiter and Cassini to Saturn. Today both Voyager spacecraft continue to return valuable science from the far reaches of our solar system. NASA/JPL-Caltech Twin Travelers In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Using six gravity assists between them, this Grand Tour gave us up-close views of the gas and ice giants, including several moons. By the 1980s, the two probes went their separate ways at Saturn. As Voyager 2 continued toward Uranus and Neptune, Voyager 1 grabbed one more portrait of the solar system (excluding Mercury and Mars), including a final image of the pale blue dot we call home. The Golden Record Cover NASA/JPL-Caltech Playlist “Hello from the children of planet Earth.” Every good road trip needs some music to match. In this case, each craft carries the Golden Record , a 12-inch phonograph record with spoken greetings in 55 languages, 27 musical tracks, 116 images, and other sounds from Earth. Each record is protected by an outer cover featuring etchings showing our Sun’s location relative to 14 pulsars, along with instructions on how to play it. The design used various metals to protect the information encoded from space radiation: the record used copper and gold plating, and the cover used aluminum. The cover was electroplated with an ultra-pure sample of the isotope uranium-238. Uranium-238 has a half-life of 4.468 billion years. Are We There Yet? Did you know that a light-minute is a measure of distance, not time? In August 2012 and November 2018, Voyager 1 and 2 crossed the heliopause, the boundary where the Sun’s solar wind meets the interstellar medium. Using NASA’s Deep Space Network , Earth communicates with both spacecraft and tracks each on its journey. At the time of this article, the Canberra antenna tracked Voyager 1 at 25.80 billion km, or just over 16 billion miles. This graphic shows the position of NASA’s Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 probes, outside of the heliosphere, a protective bubble created by the Sun that extends well past the orbit of Pluto. NASA/JPL-Caltech On November 18, 2026, 49 years after its launch, Voyager 1 will cross the one-light-day mark, 16.1 billion miles from the Sun. You may have heard the term light-year in your favorite sci-fi movie or show, or when stargazing and referring to an object outside of our solar system. This video best demonstrates the different distances between the inner solar system, outer solar system, and beyond,

item.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
item.description: null Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere. With 37 hours of JWST observations covering nearly four full orbits of TOI-561, scientists have now found this horrific planet is buried in a reflective layer of vaporized silicate mineral clouds, the same family of compounds that make up quartz and sand. "We measured how the planet's brightness and heat changed throughout its orbit," team member Lisa Dang of the University of Waterloo said in a statement. "This technique, known as a phase curve, revealed that the planet reflects a significant amount of light from its star, and that heat is being redistributed around the planet instead of only on the sunlit side. Together, these point to the presence of an atmosphere." The hemispheres of lava super-Earth are day and night The proximity of TOI-561 b to its star has another consequence. The planet is tidally locked, meaning it doesn't turn like Earth . Thus, TOI-561 b has one blisteringly hot "dayside" permanently facing its star, and a cooler "nightside" facing out into space in perpetuity. Dang and colleagues investigated the fact that the bare rock of the dayside seemed to be cooler than should be expected. They theorized that missing heat could be carried around to the night side or the heat may be reflected away before TOI-561 b can absorb it. By using the JWST to observe full orbits of TOI-561 b, the team was able to observe the planet's nightside for the first time. They found it isn't warm enough to account for all the heat missing from the dayside. That means TOI-561 b must reflect roughly three-quarters of the starlight that hits it. That is comparable to the most reflective planet in the solar system, Venus , which reflects around 75% of incident sunlight compared to the 30% reflected by Earth. The team determined that this high reflectivity is the result of clouds of silicate minerals, including silicon dioxide and magnesium silicate, forming on the planet's dayside and acting like sunscreen. These clouds could also help TOI-561 b hang on to an atmosphere. A diagram shows that TOI-561 b and its two exoplanet siblings would fit well within the orbit of Mercury around the sun (Image credit: NASA) Of course, the team can't yet be sure what this atmosphere

item.title: Scientists confirm fruit and vegetable skin really is good for you
item.description: Fruit and vegetable skin is often rich in fibre Ekaterina Vasileva-Bagler/Getty Images Some people are convinced that fruit and vegetable skin are particularly nutritious, and now scientists have confirmed the idea. They have discovered that these parts of fruits and vegetables often contain far more fibre than the flesh we normally consume. The finding suggests cooks are unwittingly discarding fibre-rich food by chucking out the seeds, skins and stems of fruits and vegetables when preparing a meal. Home cooks and caterers should adopt “root to tip” eating and start cooking with squash peel, watermelon rind and pepper stalks to improve the public’s intake of dietary fibre, the team says. Advertisement Read more Our food system is vulnerable to El Niño, warns UK climate minister “We’ve really got to shift our purchasing habits to buy whole fruits and vegetables, and then use all of the fruits and vegetables in dishes,” says Rachel Gibson at King’s College London. Gibson and her colleagues tested the fibre content of 12 fruits and vegetables, including butternut squash, kiwi fruit, watermelon, broccoli and bell pepper. The team measured the fibre content both in the parts typically consumed and the parts that usually go to waste. They found that, in 10 of the 12 produce types, the normally wasted components contain more fibre than the commonly consumed parts. Butternut squash seeds and skin, for example, contained 9.25 grams of fibre per 100 grams, compared with 2 g of fibre per 100 g of squash flesh. Meanwhile, the skin and core of a pineapple core contains 450 per cent more fibre than the flesh. These skin and core components are often tough to chew, but the researchers say they can be blended, grated or roasted to make them more palatable. Free newsletter Sign up to The Weekly Sign up to newsletter Just 4 per cent of British adults meet the recommended minimum daily intake of 30 g of dietary fibre, with the average adult consuming around half that per day. Gibson suggests caterers could use the findings to design fibre-rich meals using more produce that would otherwise go to waste. This could reduce food waste and cut costs for commercial kitchens, as well as increasing dietary fibre intake, she says. King’s College London’s canteen piloted a “root to tip” menu in May 2025. Meals included a West African peanut stew made with all of a butternut squash, kale stalks and leek tops, and a watermelon salad featuring pickled watermelon rind. Simple menu tweak can nudge people into choosing climate-friendly food Rejigging the meal choices on offer in a canteen can prompt people to make healthier, climate-friendlier decisions Eating a larger proportion of harvested fruit and vegetables will also improve the resilience of the food system in the face of climate shocks , says Gibson. “Everything we pull out of the ground that we can eat, we should be eating.” Christian Reynolds at City St George’s University of London says the research is an “exciting inves

item.title: Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi
item.description: Political economist and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Pat Utomi, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, plans to strengthen the naira to N500 per dollar if elected in 2027. In a post on X on Thursday, he said the plan to strengthen the naira from its current level of about N1,350 to N500 per dollar would help control inflation, reduce poverty and boost Nigerians’ purchasing power. “We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he wrote. “It offers a direct, multi-faceted approach to curbing inflation, reducing poverty, and lowering the cost of living.” He projected that a loaf of sliced bread currently selling for N1,750 could fall to N800, while the price of a 50kg bag of imported rice could drop from N55,000 to N27,500. Also, a medium-sized tuber of yam would decline from N2,400 to N1,200, while a 50kg bag of maize could fall from N75,000 to N37,500. Utomi further projected that a bunch of plantain would drop from N2,500 to N1,250, while the price of whole chicken could fall from N7,000 to N3,500. A dozen eggs could sell for N1,150, down from N2,300, while a painter of garri could decline from N1,300 to N650. Utomi said the proposal reflected the party’s commitment to improving living conditions, particularly for Nigerians experiencing multidimensional poverty. “It clearly demonstrates our concrete plan to uplift the 140 million Nigerians currently experiencing multi-dimensional poverty,” he added. The post Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alli faults Makinde over doctors’, lecturers’ strikes, promises workers better welfare
item.description: The All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Alli, has promised prompt payment of salaries, allowances and other entitlements to workers if elected in the 2027 governorship election. Alli also criticised Governor Seyi Makinde over the ongoing strikes by medical and dental officers in the state and lecturers at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso, accusing him of neglecting the welfare of workers and residents. The APC candidate made his position known in a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Media and Publicity of the Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation, Bisi Oladele, in Ibadan. The medical workers began their strike on Monday, while members of the LAUTECH branch of the Academic Staff Union of Universities embarked on an indefinite strike on Thursday. The campaign organisation said the industrial actions had disrupted healthcare and education services, leaving patients in public hospitals without access to essential medical attention. It faulted the state government for allowing disputes over outstanding allowances and the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement to escalate into strikes. The organisation also described the demands of the medical workers as legitimate, noting that they included payment of outstanding allowances and restoration of salaries for personnel transferred from field assignments to the Ministry of Health. It warned that the withdrawal of medical services would worsen the challenges facing public hospitals, particularly for vulnerable residents who depend on government healthcare facilities. “Every additional day of this strike raises serious concerns about access to emergency treatment, continuity of care and the welfare of vulnerable patients,” the statement said. The campaign organisation also accused Makinde of prioritising his presidential ambition over the crises in the state. “Rather than remain at his duty post to resolve a crisis that has further crippled an already struggling public healthcare and education system, the governor is busy chasing the mirage of an illusory presidential ambition,” it said. It added that “the allure of presidential power appears to have eclipsed the solemn obligations of his present office.” The organisation appealed to the striking workers to remain open to dialogue and urged the state government to make emergency arrangements to protect patients requiring urgent medical attention. It said an Alli-led administration would prioritise workers’ welfare, constructive engagement with health professionals and the provision of modern equipment and facilities in public hospitals. The post Alli faults Makinde over doctors’, lecturers’ strikes, promises workers better welfare appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US midterms: With deep-red states now in play, could blue wave redraw America's political landscape?
item.description: With the US approaching a potentially consequential midterm election, the political landscape appears to be shifting. Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Dr Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics & Policy at Queen Mary University of London, who examines the prospect of a sweeping Democratic victory. He argues that the party could achieve gains of a magnitude not seen since Barack Obama's historic presidential election in 2008. Johnson sees a combination of Democratic enthusiasm, and growing support among independents, white college-educated voters and Latinos, and signs of defections from Donald Trump's fiercely loyal electoral coalition.

item.title: UK Shelly reseller warns payment data stolen after malware found on website
item.description: A UK-based reseller of Shelly smart home equipment has warned customers that their payment data may be compromised after “unauthorized software” was found on its website. “After receiving a warning from our payment provider, Stripe, we investigated and found unauthorized software on our website and server,” the email from Shelly Store UK, seen by The Register , stated. “We removed the identified malicious software, strengthened access security, applied security updates and introduced ongoing monitoring. We have also reported the incident to the Information Commissioner’s Office .” Shelly Store UK informed customers it was unable to determine whether their data was accessed or copied, although all customers who made orders during an unspecified window are being contacted. One punter told us that hours before they received the email from Shelly Store UK, they began a payment dispute with their card provider after a £221.28 transaction, dated October 26, was made in Australia using their details. They suspect their full card details were swiped at some point between October 12, when they made their first and only order with the company, and October 27, when they received the breach notification. Shelly Store UK did not immediately respond to our request for more details. Its notification email stated the internal investigation remains ongoing, and in addition to payment card details, customers may have had their names, billing addresses, and contact details compromised. Shelly Store UK recommended that customers contact their card issuer for guidance on whether they will need a replacement card, and to scour their transaction histories and report any suspicious entries. It also urged caution in receiving communications asking for data such as payment details and security codes, and recommended a password reset . “We’re sorry for the concern and inconvenience this may cause,” the company said. “We are taking this seriously and will contact you if our investigation identifies further information relevant to you.” Shelly Store UK is an authorized reseller of Shelly smart home products and is wholly independent of the main Shelly company. “Shelly Store is a reseller of Shelly and is not part of, owned by, or directly affiliated with Shelly Group,” a Shelly spokesperson said. “We do not manage the Shelly Store website, its business operations, and we do not direct our customers from any of our websites to Shelly Store UK.” ®

item.title: In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet
item.description: Eden, the planet in Chris Beckett’s Dark Eden, drifts outside the Milky Way McCarthy's PhotoWorks/Shutterstock I came up with the idea of the planet Eden in 1992 for a short story called The Circle of Stones . At that time, I had no idea that there really were such things as planets without suns, but it seemed likely to me. It also seemed possible to me that life might arise on such a planet, since, even here on Earth, whole ecologies thrive without sunlight around thermal vents in the deep ocean. Life on Earth may have even have begun in such places. Quite often, if something seems likely, it does indeed happen. (In another book , I predicted that a US president would one day seek to take over Greenland and Canada.) Having written that story, I learned that free-floating planets did indeed exist. Being dark, they’re hard to spot, but a number have been detected using gravitational lensing . And I gather it’s not particularly controversial to think that some of them might support life (though not quite in the form that I chose to imagine it – but I’ll come to that). When creating a world for a story, I don’t usually seek to make the whole thing scientifically accurate, but I try to make it hang together in a way that feels coherent. I didn’t build Eden by doing a lot of research, but I did put a lot of thought into how it might all work. This wasn’t so I could put it all in the book – no one in Eden knows this stuff and the story is told entirely by its characters! – but so that I had something to guide my imagination and make my invented world feel coherent. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter My idea was that Eden had once been covered in ice, but its hot core meant there was liquid water below the ice in which life could come into existence. One particular kind of life form appeared, somewhat resembling tree roots, that was able to obtain additional energy by pushing deep down into hot rocks, pumping its sap through them to heat it, and then pumping it back up again, like a geothermal power station. One of the ways these organisms used this heat was to push upwards into the planet’s shell of ice, melting parts of it, feeding on the nutrients it contained, and creating more living space – and they carried on doing so until much of the surface of Eden was ice-free, and had an atmosphere that would turn out to be breathable by humans. Millions of years later, this thawed-out surface, now populated by a multitude of different life forms, became the stage on which my drama could unfold: first that early story, then another story and then the novel Dark Eden and its two sequels. In Dark Eden , a tiny community of humans, descended from stranded visitors from Earth, eke out a living using tools made of stone and wood, and try to make sense of their life as exiles from a sunlit world that lives on in folk memory, but which they can only very shakily imagine. item.title: Read an extract from Dark Eden by Chris Beckett
item.description: The New Scientist Book Club is reading Dark Eden by Chris Beckett We went out by a path that led through a big clump of flickering starflowers and then into Batwing. A whole bunch of Batwing grownups and newhairs were in their clearing banging away at a giant redlantern tree with their blackglass axes, working in the pink light of its flowers. We walked round the edge of their clearing to Family Fence, dragged away the branches at the opening, and went out into open forest. No more shelters and campfires ahead of us now: nothing but shining trees. Hmmmph, hmmmph, hmmmph , went the trees. Hmmmmmm , went forest. We walked for a waking under the light of the treelanterns, slashing down whatever birds and bats and fruit we could get as we went along, and finally stopped to rest at the big lump of rock called Lava Blob. Old Roger handed us out a gritty little seedcake each, made of ground-up starflower seeds, so we could have something in our bellies, and then we settled down with our backs against the rock, so we didn’t have to worry about leopards sneaking up behind us. There were lots of yellowlantern trees round there, which we didn’t get so much back in Family, and also yellow animals called hoppers that came bouncing out of forest on their back legs and wrung their four hands together while they looked at us with their big flat eyes and went Peep peep peep . But hoppers were no good to eat and their skins were no use either, so we just chucked stones at them to make them go away and let us sleep in peace. Advertisement Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter When we woke up, Starry Swirl was still bright bright in sky. We ate a bit of dry cake and off we went again, under redlanterns and whitelanterns and spiketrees, with flutterbyes darting and glittering all round us and bats chasing the flutterbyes and trees going hmmph, hmmph, hmmph like always, until it all blurred together into that hmmmmmmmmm that was the background of our lives. After a few miles we came to a small pool full of shiny wavyweed and all us newhairs took off our wraps and dived into the warm water for crabfish and oysters to eat. All the boys watched Tina Spiketree diving in, and they all thought how graceful she was with her long legs, and how smooth her skin was, and how much they wanted to slip with her. But when she came up she swam straight to me, and gave me a dying oyster with the bright pink light still shining out of it. “You know what they say about oysters, don’t you, John?” she said. Tom’s neck, she was pretty pretty, the prettiest in whole of Family. And she knew it well well. In another couple of hours we reached the place where Peckham Hills began to rise up out of forest of Circle Valley, and started to climb up through them by Monkey Path, which isn’t really a path, but just a way we know through the trees. item.description: …. As G100 holds second summit Nov. 9 By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Roman Catholic Cardinal John Onaiyekan has thrown his weight behind efforts by opposition parties under the G100 Coalition to present a united front ahead of the 2027 elections, as the Coalition prepares to hold its second summit on Monday, November 9, 2026. The leaders of the Coalition, comprising National Chairmen and National Secretaries of some political parties, briefed the Cardinal at his residence on Thursday in Abuja. In a statement signed on behalf of the Coalition Parties, Salihu Moh. Lukman said the leaders told His Eminence about “initiatives and efforts being made to present a united front of opposition political parties and ensure that Nigerians are presented with a credible alternative to rescue the country.” Among those who met the cardinal were the factional national chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Kabiru Tanimu Turaki SAN, and the faction’s national secretary, Honourable Daniel Woyengikuro. The Social Democratic Party SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Umar Abubakar Gombe, and the People’s Redemption Party PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba Ahmed, were also there, alongside the PRP National Secretary, Mr Sunny Kanu. Professor Jibrin Ibrahim, a civil society activist and scholar, facilitated the meeting. The Cardinal was told that work had been concluded on three working papers of the Coalition. They are “The National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, which outlined the principles of the Coalition; The Framework for Opposition Unity, which describes how the coalition will work; and The National Reform Programme, which sets out what a government built on this cooperation would seek to do for Nigerians.” According to the statement, Coalition leaders are working to conclude and adopt the papers before the Second Summit on November 9, where all the political parties under the Coalition will endorse and unveil them. The Cardinal expressed support for the efforts of opposition parties and their candidates to unite, with the aim of building “a robust opposition which is vital to the sustenance of Nigeria’s democratic traditions”. He also expressed joy that Nigerians “will have real and credible choices to enable citizens to decide their future and leaders next year.” His Eminence further stressed “the role of competent, honest and sympathetic leaders in resolving the multiple problems which combine to make the decent lives of our citizens difficult or impossible to sustain.” The delegation reported “the successes registered in attracting more parties to join the Coalition and designing mechanisms that should resolve potential sources of discord.” It also thanked the Cardinal for his “lifelong stand for justice and compassion” and asked him to continue to pray for the success of the Coalition. item.title: Netanyahu bloc finishes ahead in Israel vote, but well short of majority
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel’s general election showed Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail. The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar. Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”. The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”. – Political earthquake – The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said on Thursday. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence. Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations. Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority. “He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said. Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”. But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. item.title: Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit
item.description: A Lagos-based businessman, Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi, has confirmed that he and his company, Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited, were discharged and acquitted by the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State. Nwaobasi made the affirmation in an affidavit sworn before a Notary Public of Nigeria in Satellite Town, Lagos. Nwaobasi and his company had been charged in a five-count amended charge filed on November 21, 2024, involving allegations of conspiracy to possess hard drugs and money laundering. In an affidavit of facts dated August 4, 2026, and made available to journalists, Nwaobasi identified himself as the first defendant in Charge No. FHC/UM/CR/143/2024, between the Federal Republic of Nigeria and Nwaobasi Kelechi Monday (also known as Nwaobasi Kelechi Michael, “Aboy”) and Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited. He stated that, on May 29, 2025, the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State, discharged and acquitted him and his company, the second defendant in the case. According to him, the order was made by the Federal High Court, Umuahia, presided over by Honourable Justice K. O. Ogundare. He explained that the affidavit was required for official and record purposes. “I swear to this affidavit in good faith, believing same to be true and correct to the best of my knowledge in accordance with the Oaths Law of Lagos State 2015,” Nwaobasi stated. In its ruling, the court held that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Nwaobasi and his company on any of the five counts. The judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution was insufficient to warrant calling on the defendants to enter their defence to the charges. “In sum, I find that no prima facie case has been made out against the defendants by the prosecution in all the counts as the prosecution has failed to prove the elements of the offence in each of the counts. “Consequently, the no case submission is hereby upheld and the defendants are hereby discharged and acquitted on each of the 1st -5th counts of the offence charged by virtue of Section 357 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015,” the judge held in a ruling delivered in open court. The certified true copy of the ruling made available to journalists listed E. C. Onyema-Opara, Esq., as counsel for the prosecution, while V. A. Ekwegh, Esq., and O. E. Porbeni, Esq., were listed as counsel for the defendants. The post Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adamu makes history as first Nigerian CAF General Secretary
item.description: Nigerian football administrator Samson Adamu has been confirmed as the substantive General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), becoming the first Nigerian to occupy the position in the organisation’s 70-year history. The confirmation was announced on Thursday, with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) congratulating Adamu on his appointment. The NFF’s acting general secretary, Emmanuel Ikpeme, described the development as a significant moment for Nigerian football administration and expressed confidence in Adamu’s ability to excel in the role. “This is, indeed, very good news. I am so happy for Samson Adamu on his confirmation, and I know he is going to make Nigeria and Africa proud,” Ikpeme said. “The NFF is delighted with this appointment, and we will give him all the necessary support as a member association under CAF. We wish him tremendous success in the job,” Ikpeme added. Adamu joined CAF, the continent’s football governing body headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, as Director of Competitions before becoming Director of Tournaments and Events. He was appointed acting general secretary on March 29 following the resignation of his predecessor, Veron Mosengo-Omba, a Swiss-Congolese football administrator. Adamu holds a FIFA Master’s degree in the management, law and humanities of sport. He began his career in football administration by establishing the now-defunct Copa Lagos beach soccer tournament in the early 2010s. The post Adamu makes history as first Nigerian CAF General Secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products. It nevertheless insisted: “User funds are completely safe.” Several experts said it looked like a massive amount of assets had been stolen. “It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder. Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea. Bitcoin prices fell more than three percent on the news. The post Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle. The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026. The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition. CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable. In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation’s 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent. “The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa,” he said. Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition. He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future. Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament. The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year. Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries’ ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027. He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa’s cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together. “The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa’s rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa’s 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world,” he said. “The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa,” he added. The post AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night. The attackers were said to have stormed the community at about 8pm and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to check attacks and restore security. A resident of Barkin Ladi, Mr Bulus Jok, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen struck the community around 8pm despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically.” Jok said, “They were shooting at anything they saw. The attack created panic in the community, and four people were killed.” He added, “The incident is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack.” Also confirming the incident, Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Mr Rwang Tengwong, said, “Terrorist gangs reportedly attacked Sabon Angwa, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, and shot four people dead.” Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, adding, “We condemn this latest attack in strong terms and lament the loss of these lives.” He said, “It is disturbing that communities are still being attacked despite the security measures and curfew put in place to protect residents.” The BYM spokesman urged security operatives to intensify surveillance and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities, saying, “We call on security agencies to strengthen their presence and respond promptly to early warning alerts.” Efforts to reach security operatives for more details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen kill four in Plateau community appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Google's search revenue Ferrari hits an AI-powered speed bump
item.description: Google is paying a higher price for its bet on AI than even Alphabet's $51.4 billion in Q3 capital expenditures suggest. The biz appears to have traded its high-performing search advertising business for the mediocre monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode, a misstep that contributed to investor concerns as Alphabet lost roughly $500 billion in market value despite management's attempts to reassure Wall Street. Google's year-over-year search revenue growth slowed from 17 percent in Q2 to 12 percent in Q3 . It's still headed in the right direction, but at a slower rate. During Alphabet's conference call for investors, Douglas Anmuth from JPMorgan Chase & Co asked whether that's because Google is showing fewer ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode than it shows in its traditional search results. Chief business officer Philipp Schindler cited several reasons for that: foreign exchange rates, Europe's elimination of its customs-duty exemption, and "the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode." To compensate, Google said it is expanding the distribution of AI Overview ads and adding multiturn ads in the US for AI Mode queries. But some Google Ads customers appear to be more concerned about quality than quantity. In a social media post , Max Anderson, CEO of OnlyFinder, complained that Google has responded to declining search volumes by attempting to manufacture revenue growth through "short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics," such as charging advertisers more for lower-quality clicks, including clicks on search terms they had not agreed to target. Eric Seufert, an analyst with Mobile Dev Memo, dismissed the doomsayers in a blog post . "It’s tempting to look at the successive deceleration in Search revenue growth from Q1 2026 as a response to pressure from other chatbots and to assume that Search query volume is migrating elsewhere," he wrote. "But the earnings release notes that the 'year-over-year Search query growth rate [was] the highest it has been in the last five years' in Q3, so it's clear that Search usage isn't declining." So people are still searching, and the business is still growing, but less convincingly, thanks to the lower monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode. And Google's answer involves more ads in AI interactions. Nate Elliott, principal analyst for AI at Emarketer, told The Register in an email that AI represents a double-edged sword for Google's ad business. "On the one hand, Google owns the thing that people use AI for most: search," Elliott wrote. "Our surveys say that by far the top reason people use AI is to look for facts and information. Luckily for Google, people also tell us they haven't stopped using search engines – they've simply added AI as a new behavior on top of search. That means people spend more time than ever looking for information, and most of those people don't even think twice before doing their searches on Google. item.title: The 12 strangest science stories we can’t stop thinking about
item.description: The warty comb jelly has an anus that comes and goes Andrey Nekrasov/imageBROKER.com​/Alamy There are some stories that stay with you forever, the big scientific moments that change the course of history. These are not those moments – but we can’t stop thinking about them anyway. Push my button Surgeon Stuart Meloy was performing a pain-relief operation on a woman’s spine when she started exclaiming emphatically. “You’re going to have to teach my husband to do that,” the woman said. This inspired Meloy to invent an implant to help women who are unable to achieve orgasms in the usual way. New Scientist broke the news in 2001, sparking a frenzy of worldwide media excitement. But 13 years later, Meloy was still struggling to raise funds for a full clinical trial, and the “orgasmatron” never reached a climax. Monkey pleasure A long-tailed macaque Shutterstock/fiz_zero We aren’t the only primates capable of coming up with creative ways to pleasure ourselves. In a study of long-tailed macaques ( Macaca fascicularis ) in Bali, Indonesia, Camilla Cenni at the University of Lethbridge in Alberta, Canada, and her colleagues filmed hundreds of examples of male and female monkeys using stone tools as sex toys , rubbing or tapping them on their genitals. According to Cyril Grueter at the University of Western Australia, the Balinese monkeys get plenty of food handouts from humans, and this frees up time for sexual experimentation. But some monkeys in other places have unusual kinks, too: another study reported a wild macaque in Japan rubbing its genitals on the back of a sika deer. Advertisement Head transplants In 2015, surgeon Sergio Canavero announced plans to carry out the first human head transplant, intended to extend the lives of people with muscle and nerve degeneration or widespread cancer. He claimed his technique could overcome technical hurdles, including how to fuse the spinal cord and prevent the body’s immune system from rejecting the head. In the following two years, Canavero published animal experiments supposedly backing up his methods, but other surgeons remained highly sceptical . A human head transplant never did happen, but Canavero has reportedly moved on to an even bolder ambition: transplanting a brain into a non-sentient clone. Rats driving Have you ever wondered if a rat can drive a car? Kelly Lambert at the University of Richmond in Virginia has. She and her colleagues built a tiny car with three copper bars that would steer it left, forward or right. Sure enough, 18 rats learned to drive towards food rewards. They even found it relaxing, as measurements of their stress hormones indicated. Lambert proposed that driving challenges could replace traditional maze tests when using rat models to study neuropsychiatric conditions. The sniff test Humans are more similar to rats than we like to think.
