item.title: Serial ransomware crook gets 70 months behind bars for Nefilim, Hive roles
item.description: Ukrainian ransomware crook Artem Stryzhak has been sentenced to 70 months in the slammer by a New York federal court for his role as an affiliate of the Nefilim and Hive ransomware gangs. Prosecutors believe the cybercriminal began working with Nefilim in or around June 2021, while living in Barcelona, Spain. The Nefilim ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation was known for targeting wealthy companies, with its operators encouraging affiliates to pursue businesses capable of paying substantial ransom demands. One of Nefilim's most high-profile attacks was on Australian logistics giant Toll Group in 2020, encrypting its files roughly three months after it suffered a separate Mailto ransomware attack. Court documents [PDF] state that Stryzhak agreed with alleged Nefilim boss Volodymyr Tymoshchuk , who remains at large, to pay the ransomware crew a 20 percent cut of the ransom proceeds he collected. Tymoshchuk told Stryzhak that his preference was for attacks to target companies based in the US, Canada, and Australia that turn over more than $100 million annually. This guidance was soon tweaked to encourage targeting companies in the same regions with more than $200 million in annual revenue. Prosecutors claim that around the time Stryzhak joined forces with Nefilim, he also signed up to the Hive ransomware operation as "one of its earliest affiliates," and used its platform to attack approximately seven victims. Hive's operators claimed they targeted circa 1,500 victims worldwide between June 2021 and January 2023. According to separate court documents [PDF], Hive's victims included a law firm and an Ohio hospital, which paid approximately $1.7 million in Bitcoin after the gang initially demanded $2 million during the COVID-19 pandemic. Before its infrastructure was seized in an international law enforcement operation in January 2023, Hive was known for attacking healthcare facilities during the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as being one of the ransomware groups that battered Costa Rica in 2022 . Brett Leatherman, assistant director at the FBI’s cyber branch, described Stryzhak as a “prolific cybercriminal” who played a role in groups that were responsible for more than $100 million in victim damages. “Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak’s crimes and demonstrates the FBI’s global reach and extensive network of international partners,” he said. “Multiple field offices contributed to this investigation, and our work does not end here. We will continue to leverage every tool at our disposal to track down Stryzhak’s co-conspirators and hold them accountable, including Volodymyr Viktorovych Tymoshchuk.” Stryzhak was arrested by Spanish police in June 2024 before being extradited to the US in April 2025. item.title: China's secretive space plane caught on camera in incredible new photo released by US military
item.description: null A photograph of China's reusable Shenlong space plane docked to another spacecraft, taken by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite from a distance of 56 miles (90 kilometers). (Image credit: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor) A U.S. military intelligence agency has released an incredible new photograph of China's secretive space plane, showing it docked to another spacecraft in orbit. The photograph was taken in 2024 by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite, from a distance of 56 miles (90 kilometers). Ground-based observers have previously photographed Shenlong in orbit , but this new photo from Vantor, taken from space, reveals new details about the mysterious spacecraft in stunning clarity, with a resolution of 4.5 centimeters (1.8 inches) per pixel. The image was included in a new report released by the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) assessing the scope and breadth of adversary threats in space. In the image, the robotic Shenlong space plane can be seen docked to another satellite that has its solar panels deployed. It's not yet known which satellite that may have been. Shenlong's payload bay doors can also be seen in the photograph, in an open position. Those payload doors may offer clues about what Shenlong is doing on its fourth mission, which launched in February 2026 . China's space agency has stated only that Shenlong helps test technologies that "will pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space in the future." But observers have seen Shenlong release other objects while in orbit, such as in June 2026, when American space intelligence company LeoLabs reported that itdetected a new object in the vicinity of the space plane. "Following additional observations across our global network and analysis via LeoLabs Delta, we have independently cataloged this object and assessed with high confidence that it was released from the Chinese space plane," LeoLabs stated at the time. "This activity is consistent with sub-satellite deployments conducted by the space plane in previous missions." A similar event happened during Shenlong's third mission , which ended in 2024. On its second mission in 2023, the space plane also released an object and may have conducted what are known as proximity and rendezvous operations, in which two spacecraft maneuver close to one another. It may have been that the spacecraft was releasing unnecessary hardware before landing, however. Like all things military space, few details have been released to the public about Shenlong's operations. The United States, similarly, operates a secretive robotic space plane, the Boeing-built X-37B , and rarely releases concrete details about its capabilities or its missions. In February 2025, the U.S. Space Force released its first photo of the X-37B in space, offering a rare glimpse at the space plane in operation. The photo appeared to show it in a high Earth orbit with what appear to be its payload bay doors open. In 2023, Space Force relea

item.title: How Google fumbled the frontend with Angular 2
item.description: A cartoon from an ex-Google software engineer, titled “Welcome to Google,” made the rounds a while back. It featured two diverging roads, neither passable. One was the main road, marked as deprecated (“don’t even think about it,” the sign read). The new road, however, was marked as still under construction (“Danger”), and so was unusable as well. That was the no-win choice two million frontend developers faced in 2014, when Google unexpectedly deprecated its popular JavaScript framework, AngularJS, in favor of Angular 2, which had a radically different architecture, a confusing name, no upgrade path, and wasn’t even fully released yet. So, many developers turned the wheel and headed to Reactville or Vuetown instead. How Google botched the Angular upgrade provides timely lessons in how not to update a software package, which former Google Developer Advocate Stephen Fluin outlined in a talk at the All Things Open conference last week. “Uncertainty kills motivation,” said Fluin. “When you're taking away everything [developers] know and love, they're going to feel disheartened.” Fluin is now head of developer relations for Buildkite , but he worked for Google from 2016 to 2021 on the Angular project. “Things were a little bit rough at the time. It was a bit of a death march,” he told the audience. “We had no idea when Angular 2 was going to come out, and the core fundamentals of Angular kept changing.” From AngularJS to Angular 2 Google had good reasons for updating Angular. The AngularJS team had been snatched from Google’s infrastructure division and placed under its ad division, where the software could be more fully exploited. To support operations of that size, Angular needed greater rigor. The original AngularJS was launched in 2009 as a side project of Google engineer Miško Hevery , who wanted to extend HTML. Google pulled AngularJS into an internal project because Google developers found it easier to work with than the Java-based Google Web Toolkit ( GWT ). The framework quickly caught on with outside web developers too, who readily understood the angle brackets of HTML (hence the name) and wanted more interactive components. Hevery built AngularJS 1.3 with a traditional controller model, which handled all user input, logic and data transport under the JavaScript $scope object. Angular 2, announced at the ng-europe 2014 conference, was a major shift in architecture. It shifted to a component model, with each HTML template enjoying its own class properties. After a forced, unhappy dalliance with Google's Dart , the team rewrote Angular completely in TypeScript, with no backward compatibility whatsoever. It was a lot to take in, and the introductory talk at ng-europe seemed to spook Angular developers more than inspire them. For each discarded feature, the speakers displayed a graphic of a tombstone (“RIP Controllers”) and played a recording of a church bell tolling in the background. “That talk is still infamous today for what it did to the co

item.title: Social media is full of weird video game mashups. Where are they all coming from?
item.description: AI tools are making it easier to modify and recreate games, raising questions about piracy, copyright and how far the technology could disrupt the industry • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games . Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from. Of course, the answer – or at least, most of the answer – is AI. After a week of researching this (thanks especially to Replay Mode on YouTube for this informative video , which set me down this track) I now understand that these mashup mods are not just AI-generated videos, but AI-assisted coding. Basically, as of a few weeks ago, Anthropic’s Claude has become extremely good at decompiling video game code. Games are written by humans in readable code and then compiled into binary 1s and 0s that the PC or console running it can read; decompiling is the reversal of that process, revealing a game’s source code, which humans can then edit and mess around with for fun. This used to be an extremely laborious process. But now it is not, because humans aren’t doing much of it any more. Continue reading...

item.title: The final ‘Dune: Part Three’ trailer reignites war on Arrakis and leaves us with more questions than answers
item.description: Dune: Part Three 's marketing campaign has been a long and generous one, but Warner Bros. and Legendary Pictures knew an extra push was needed in order to compete with Avengers: Doomsday , as both sci-fi blockbusters will be releasing next to each other at Christmas. In its final trailer, Denis Villeneuve's threequel goes all out. This isn't the first time a Dune: Part Three trailer has left us with more questions than answers , but the in-depth look at the character dynamics and plot beats that await will make longtime fans of Frank Herbert's works raise their eyebrows. Messiah, the second installment in the book series, is a novel of long monologues and very tense conversations. Action has a place in it, but it's a more restrained and quieter book for the most part — one that deals with the consequences of Paul's (now a space dictator) originally well-meaning actions. Of course, the cinematic medium requires a very different language, especially when the main reason why these movies have become blockbuster hits is that Villeneuve has expertly balanced the drama and large-scale action. So, it comes as no surprise that his take on Messiah is looking to bring Herbert's concluding thoughts on Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) to life without sacrificing the grandeur that defined the first two movies. More shocking to readers, of course, is Zendaya's (Chani) much larger role in this finale versus the book, where she was slightly sidelined with a more passive part. Paul's lover walking away from him at the end of Part Two was a major departure, and one that set her up for bigger things in the third entry. Considering how good Zendaya has been in the role so far, we consider this a win... unless Villeneuve completely bungles her arc in the final stretch. Dune: Part Three emerges from the sand of Arrakis on December 18, 2026, only in cinemas. item.title: Eko Hotels at 50: A Defining Moment for African Hospitality on the Global Stage
item.description: The Legacy Gala & Awards night : Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity. 2nd of October 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history, others are built to make it. For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre . Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it. The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality. But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance. This was not merely a party, It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow, Fifty years of memories finding their voices, Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa a nd for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance. A Hotel Became Part of a Nation’s Story There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory, Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter. Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families. Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalized. For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world, f or others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos. Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership. Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation, It must become an experience, a cultural encounter, a n economic opportunity, a reason to travel and reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for. The Night Africa Wore Her Crown The Legacy Gala & Awards night brought together more than 1,000 distinguished guests, representing an extraordinary convergence of business, government, entertainment, culture and society. Among the dignitaries were Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu , Deputy Governor Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat , prominent business leaders, industry executives, ce

item.title: Microsoft faces potential vote: Shareholders curious about its plans to tackle emissions
item.description: Trillium Asset Management wants Microsoft to explain how it will meet its 2030 greenhouse gas (GHG) emission targets, and is backing a shareholder proposal to request this information at the firm’s next shareholder meeting. The cloud and software biz set itself lofty environmental goals back in 2020 , aiming to be become "carbon-negative" by 2030, and to have removed the equivalent of all the carbon it has ever emitted by 2050. But since the start of the decade, an explosion in AI development and demand for ever more complex models has seen a boom in demand for high-performance compute infrastructure and a construction wave to deliver new datacenters to house it all in. Microsoft is one of the firms to profit from this huge demand, with its cloud division making $214.4 billion in revenue for the fiscal year 2026 ended June 30, a 27 percent year-on-year increase. This has also caused Microsoft’s emissions to head in the wrong direction, with figures from the company’s most recent Environmental Sustainability Report showing that these have increased from 13 million tons of CO 2 equivalent in 2020 to 20 million tons in 2025. However, Microsoft estimates that without the carbon reduction initiatives it has already put in place, emissions would now be much higher, somewhere near 34 million tons. The increase is largely accounted for by indirect emissions (Scope 3) from the construction and provisioning of datacenters to meet that demand for cloud services and AI training. But as The Register pointed out, 2025 saw a growing contribution from Scope 2, due to generation of energy the company purchased. This represents 13 percent of total emissions – up from 2 percent in 2024. Now Trillium Asset Management, financial advisors specializing in sustainable and responsible investing, is urging Microsoft shareholders to vote for Proposal 4 during their annual meeting scheduled for December 8. In an SEC filing , the proposal asks Microsoft to disclose additional information illustrating how it will manage climate commitments. This disclosure should go beyond existing disclosures, at reasonable cost, omitting proprietary information, and be made annually. The proposal notes that when Microsoft first announced its carbon negative goal, it said progress required "not just a bold goal but a detailed plan," and that transparency was one of the guiding principles for this climate plan. It states that emissions are now 62 percent above the 2020 baseline, and simply asks Microsoft to apply the principles it articulated in 2020; show the plan, be candid about the math, and explain how it will adapt. In the filing, Trillium warns that falling short of its climate targets may create risk to Microsoft’s credibility, which can influence investor trust. If Microsoft is in danger of failing to meet its 2030 commitments, it could suffer reputational harm, and the filing claims it is already the subject of legal action by investors alleging insufficient disclosure of its AI and

item.title: Satellites watch an escaping Antarctic iceberg | Space photo of the day for Oct. 28, 2026
item.description: null Iceberg A-81 escaping the Weddell Sea and drifting near the edge of South Georgia's underwater shelf. The image was captured on Oct. 20, 2026. (Image credit: NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison) An iceberg has quickly escaped from the Weddell Sea in Antarctica, on its way to an icy new destination. What is it? As captured by a satellite in orbit, the Antarctic iceberg A-81 has quite quickly (for an iceberg) parted ways from its icy home, breaking off to drift toward a shallow underwater shelf in Georgia. The 600-square-mile (1,550-square-kilometer) iceberg first broke off from the Brunt Ice Shelf in January of 2023. Now, generally speaking, giant icebergs don't travel that fast. But In just three years, this massive iceberg has traveled 1,400 miles (2,300 kilometers) north of the Brunt Ice Shelf. For an iceberg, that's really fast. Over this time period, the iceberg drifted through the Weddell Sea in Antarctica's Southern Ocean before reaching the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula, floating further into the Scotia Sea and then finally now reaching the edge of a remote island in South Georgia. In this satellite snapshot captured on Oct. 20, 2026, we can see the iceberg in its current location near an underwater shelf off the coast of South Georgia. While it isn't abnormal for icebergs like A-81 to break off from larger ice shelves, Brunt has recently had multiple large icebergs break off one quickly after the other, according to a statement from NASA . Why is it incredible? This image was captured by the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), an instrument on board NASA's Terra satellite. Earth -observing satellites like Terra keep a close eye on changes on our home planet. In addition to this image, observations from Terra have showed how the iceberg has traveled over the last few years. With satellites like Terra, scientists can keep a close eye on these changes in Antarctic ice, which is becoming increasingly important as climate change continues to progress across the globe, affecting everything from Arctic ice to sea levels rising, worsening natural disasters and more.

item.title: China's spaceplane bears striking resemblance to America's X-37B
item.description: China's secretive spaceplane has been spotted in orbit by a US commercial satellite, according to the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) The DIA's report [PDF] warns of developments by China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea that allegedly threaten space security, at least from a US perspective. Most of the report details systems still under development, but one image on page 53 stands out: China's spaceplane, snapped in orbit in 2024 by Maxar Technologies. The image has been seen before; a low-resolution snap from an industry symposium was shared by Bluesky user @dutchspace almost two years ago. However, the higher-resolution image in the DIA report shows more detail. The spaceplane also bears a distinct resemblance to the US Space Force's X-37B. The uncrewed X-37 began as a NASA project in 1999 before the US Department of Defense took over. After several atmospheric tests with an X-37A variant, the X-37B was launched in 2010. The reusable spaceplane can spend years in orbit, conducting classified activities. So far, it has launched eight times. According to the DIA's report, China's first spaceplane mission launched in 2020 and remained in orbit for two days. A second, launched in 2022, spent 276 days in orbit, and a third, launched in December 2023, spent 268 days in oribt. The last two missions appeared to include approach and rendezvous tests of objects in orbit. Russia, memorably, had a spaceplane in the ill-fated Buran, which bore an uncanny resemblance to the US Space Shuttle (although the two were very different beasts from a technical perspective – not least, Buran's orbiter did not carry the engines used to launch it to space). However, according to the DIA's report, Russia "has made little progress since." The US recently confirmed that it has weapons in space, and it would be naive not to assume rivals would have their own, whether kinetic or some form of jamming technology. Earlier this month, Russia's Kosmos-2612 sidled up to the US ICEYE-X36 satellite before retreating. It's unclear whether the intention was an entirely innocent look at a fellow spacecraft or a bit of saber-rattling; it certainly worried US lawmakers . ®

item.title: Yinka Ogunbiyi Shows HaloBraid’s Automated Hair-Braiding Technology in New Demo
item.description: Harvard graduate Yinka Ogunbiyi, creator of the automated HaloBraid device engineered to complete braids up to five times faster. What if you could get your braids done in a fraction of the usual time and still leave the salon with the style you wanted? A new demonstration of HaloBraid, the automated braiding device created by Nigerian-American engineer and Harvard graduate Yinka Ogunbiyi , gives us a closer look at how that could work. Designed to help professional hairdressers braid hair up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain that comes with hours of styling, HaloBraid is now being demonstrated in action. And the interesting part is that the machine doesn’t do everything. The stylist still plays an important role in the process. Here’s how it works. The stylist sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. HaloBraid then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, while the stylist returns to finish and seal the ends. This means the machine takes care of a time-consuming part of the process, with the stylist still responsible for creating the final hairstyle. For Yinka, the idea behind HaloBraid comes from a very personal experience. Sharing the story behind the invention, she said: My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain. As a biomechanical engineer, I knew there had to be a better way, so we built HaloBraid with stylists from the beginning, bringing together inventors, designers, and builders behind some of the world’s most loved hair and beauty products. HaloBraid was built for my mum, my stylists, my aunties, and people around the world who know what it means to spend hours in the chair. The company has also secured $7 million in seed funding, with the investment round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian , who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams . With the newly shared demonstration, HaloBraid is showing how its technology works alongside professional stylists, combining hand-braiding techniques with automated weaving to reduce the time and physical effort involved in protective hairstyling. item.title: Astronomers found a mysterious object beyond Neptune, and it could be a new dwarf planet
item.description: null The powerful Vera Rubin Observatory has spotted what seems to be a dwarf planet circling the sun in the frigid depths beyond Neptune. The icy object, known as 2026 ED138, is likely between 600 and 1500 kilometers (373 to 972 miles) wide, scientists say. It's therefore probably big enough to be sculpted into a sphere by its own gravity — a key characteristic that separates dwarf planets from asteroids and other small space rocks. And if 2026 ED138 is indeed a dwarf planet, that's a pretty big deal, as astronomers have confirmed just five of them to date: Pluto , Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake . An illustration of the solar system showing the orbital pathway of newly discovered dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138 (ED138). (Image credit: NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory/NOIRLab/SLAC/AURA/R. ProctorImage Processing: M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)Orbit data provided by the IAU Minor Planet Center (MPCorb catalog), funded by NASA PDCO and the Tamkin Foundation.Star map: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio. Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC) 2026 ED138 was discovered by Matthew Holman, who works at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian (CfA). The big moment came on Oct. 13, when Holman was running previously collected Rubin data through a search code that he developed with his CfA colleague Kevin Napier. That search revealed a mysterious object beyond Neptune 's orbit. Despite its immense distance from the sun , this body was relatively bright, suggesting that it's larger than the average trans-Neptunian object. "My first reaction was one of excited disbelief," Holman said in a statement on Tuesday (Oct. 27), the day the discovery of 2026 ED138 was announced. "Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong." Those checks involved a thorough search through Rubin's catalog. And that catalog is pretty heft, even though Rubin is a pretty new scope. This image shows the orbital pathway of the newly discovered dwarf planet candidate 2026 ED138, as observed by the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory. This image is a composite of multiple images captured by Rubin between March 4 and July 11, 2026 at intervals indicated by the teal circles. ED138 is visible at the center of each circle. (Image credit: NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory/NOIRLab/SLAC/AURA. Acknowledgement: Image Processing: M. Jurić (UW), D. de Martin & M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab)) The Vera Rubin Observatory sits atop Cerro Pachón, an 8,799-foot-tall (2,682 meters) mountain in northern Chile, and features a primary mirror 28 feet (8.4 m) wide. The scope achieved first light in April 2025 and began its main project, the 10-year-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), in June of this year. During the LSST, Rubin images the entire southern sky every few days using a 3.2-gigapixel camera, the largest digital camera ever built for astronomy. This work creates a high-resolution time-lapse "movie" that can re

item.title: Intel gets tax breaks while local authorities lose revenue, claims policy org
item.description: Intel has become the latest target for Good Jobs First, which questions why the chipmaker continues to receive tax breaks from key states, long after setting up shop there, and laying off thousands of workers in those regions. The non-profit organization, which promotes accountability in economic development, says the chipmaker promised billions of dollars in investment and thousands of high-tech jobs for the areas surrounding its manufacturing plants in Hillsboro, Oregon, and Rio Rancho, New Mexico. Its report, The Bleeding Edge: How the Public Pays the Costs of Intel’s Semiconductor Manufacturing , claims that Intel's property tax breaks cost these communities more than $1.2 billion in lost revenue since 2015, and the brunt of the shortfall has largely fallen on schools funded by those local governments. For Oregon, Good Jobs First says that property tax abatements from Intel's use of the Strategic Investment Program (SIP) exempted it from at least $1.14 billion, while Hillsboro schools lost $891 million in revenue from 2017 through 2025. During the same timeframe, Intel paid Oregon $552.4 million in fees, or less than a third of the value of its tax breaks. In New Mexico, the figures are lower, but still significant. The report puts Chipzilla's property tax exemptions from Industrial Revenue Bonds (IRBs) at $99.6 million in foregone revenue since 2017, while Rio Rancho’s Public Schools lost an estimated $43.4 million over the same nine-year period. Here, the company paid $41.6 million in required payments in lieu of taxes from 2017 through 2025, shared among affected local governments. Good Jobs First also notes that despite these subsidies, Intel was awarded billions under the CHIPS Act funding from the US federal government. However, the situation with that is somewhat complex, as the company secured an initial $7.86 billion under the Biden administration, of which $2.2 billion is believed to have been paid out. The incoming Trump administration, however, decided to rethink the scheme , and ended up making an $8.9 billion deal for 10 percent of Intel’s common stock , made up of the remaining $5.7 billion of the CHIPS Act cash plus an additional $3.2 billion under the Secure Enclave program to make semiconductors for the military. At the same time, the chipmaker is estimated by Good Jobs First to have laid off more than 4,700 workers at its facilities in Oregon and New Mexico over the past three years, as the company wrestled with restructuring efforts and dramatic losses. (These are just a fraction of Intel’s total layoffs during the period.) The issue, according to the non-profit, is that these sites are established Intel facilities which the company has operated for decades. They already have the facilities, infrastructure, skilled workers, and other necessities that a new site might require investment for. item.title: Cisco open sources tool for detecting AI agents on hacking sprees
item.description: Cisco has open sourced a behavior detection engine that watches AI agents, to help security teams prevent rogue agents from going off the rails like they did with the Hugging Face hack – or worse. It’s called Project Quarry , and it aims to provide a “shared language” for evaluating agent behavior, along the lines of what Snort , which Cisco also maintains, did for detecting malicious network traffic and what YARA did for rule-based malware identification. Most detection tools rely on specific interactions with an AI model or agent. Did it attempt prompt injection? Or did the agent call an attack tool? “But what is missing is the entire context under which something may occur,” Amy Chang, head of AI threat and security research at Cisco, said in an exclusive interview with The Register . She likened this to credit card fraud detection. Without context, individual transactions such as a small test charge or a single purchase in a location far away from a card-holder's usual location may not raise any flags. “And then you try again,” making another fraudulent purchase, “and that went through, too. So now I’m gonna buy the PS5,” Chang said. “Those are the things that Quarry addresses by taking into consideration the entire agent session,” she explained. “One tool call may seem in-scope until you realize that that next step is taking that information and sending it to an attacker-controlled inbox or server.” Even data theft is a sequence and not a single agentic action. Agentic AI security firm Invariant Labs demonstrated this with a proof-of-concept attack against GitHub's MCP server that hijacked a user's agent via a malicious GitHub Issue, and coerced it into leaking data from private repositories. Simply reading a configuration file, or sending a request to an external endpoint may be legitimate agentic actions. However, combining the two can lead to data exfiltration – and shows “why action relationships matter,” wrote Chang and fellow Cisco researchers Adam Swanda, Ravikumar Balakrishnan, and Konstantin Berlin in a blog post about Quarry shared with The Register ahead of publication “A policy can produce a finding when the trace shows a sensitive file read followed within a defined window by an external send,” they wrote. “The risk comes from the relationship between the two actions, so the finding should preserve evidence from both." Quarry covers single- and multi-turn large language model conversations, agents, tool use, Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions, and multimodal inputs. In addition to the open source code itself, the project’s GitHub repository includes installation instructions, supported Python versions, plugins for Claude Code, Codex and other MCP-compatible agents, configuration examples, rule-writing guidance, and a rule starter pack. For instance, with the rule pack, “If a base-64 encoded malware is somewhere in the tool call, that would result in a block,” Chang said. The rule format looks similar to a YARA or Snort ru

item.title: Virgin Galactic is finally revealing its new Delta-class spaceship this week
item.description: null Update for 4 p.m. ET on Oct. 28: Virgin Galactic unveiled its first Delta-class space plane on Wednesday (Oct. 28), revealing that it's named Apeiron. You can read about it here . Space tourists and citizen astronauts rejoice! A new suborbital spacecraft is about to be introduced that will fly ticketholders on brief, suborbital journeys just above Earth. Virgin Galactic plans to unveil its first Delta-class spaceship on Wednesday (Oct. 28), before transporting the spacecraft from Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico. Alongside that reveal, the company will also announce the spacecraft's name, selected through a public vote held across more than 80 countries. Following its debut, the Delta-class vehicle will journey to the spaceport attached to Virgin Galactic's VMS Eve carrier aircraft, marking a transition from assembly to the beginning of official flight testing. "The arrival of our lead Spaceship at Spaceport America will be an enormous milestone in a years-long journey to build the world's first human spaceship platform designed for regular commercial spaceflight," said Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier in a statement . Virgin Galactic is targeting mid-2027 for the spacecraft's first commercial spaceflight. Simultaneously, the company is also working on a second Delta-class vehicle, which it hopes to enter into service before the end of next year. And, with the first Delta vehicle leaving the nest, the company's Mesa factory is shifting focus to the completion of the second which will lead to structural testing and preparations for its rocket engine assembly. Virgin Galactic announced its Delta manufacturing plans in 2022, initially anticipating research flights to begin in late 2025 and passenger service in 2026. Those plans have since run into multiple delays. The company said its revised schedule allows for the additional time needed to integrate and validate the spacecraft's avionics software, with final testing to take place at Spaceport America. Its Delta vehicle will replace Virgin's earlier spaceplane model, VSS Unity, which began operations in June 2023, and completed seven commercial missions before its final flight on June 8, 2024. Virgin suspended Unity's commercial flights to concentrate on developing the next-generation fleet, which is designed to carry more passengers and fly considerably more frequently. The view from Virgin Galactic's VSS Unity vehicle during one of its trips to suborbital space. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) Each Delta-class vehicle is equipped to accommodate up to six passengers, compared with Unity's four, and is expected to complete as many as eight spaceflights per month — more than 10 times the rate Virgin was flying Unity. When Virgin Galactic began selling seats aboard its planned spaceplane in 2004, tickets cost about $200,000 apiece. By 2014, nearly 700 people had reserved spots on future flights. item.title: 123 Reg discloses 'AI cyberattack' on customer data, suspects China nexus
item.description: UK domain registrar 123 Reg ( no relation – Ed ) says it was the victim of an “AI-driven cyberattack” that exposed customer data. Customers began receiving their notification emails this week, informing them that their contact information, "related customer relationship data," company VAT numbers, and "product information from an application programming interface (API)" were compromised. A company spokesperson elaborated, saying this means that names, phone numbers, countries, language and currency preferences, account creation dates, the products on the account, and marketing preferences were affected. 123 Reg described the September 18 intrusion as "the first known AI-driven cyberattack against our company," and told The Register that early signs point toward a China-nexus attacker. "Our investigation identified IP addresses that we assessed to be the core attacker infrastructure, which were hosted in China and Singapore, indicating a strong Chinese nexus," the spokesperson said. "Our investigation further identified AI cyberattack 'skills' hosted on Chinese infrastructure, including copies of skills open sourced by Anthropic and several other AI exploitation frameworks and scripts." They went on to say that many of the artefacts left behind led 123 Reg to suspect that a Chinese state-sponsored group, known for abusing Claude Code in attacks against at least 30 organizations, could be behind the break-in. There is also a suspicion that the same group that hit a number of South Korea’s financial institutions using open-source Chinese AI tool ARTEX, was behind the attack on 123 Reg too. "The TA's mirror of 'anthropic_skills,' and the account naming conventions found on the Chinese servers are consistent with preparation of this class of AI-augmented operation," the spokesperson told us. "In addition, on October 7, 2026, CrowdStrike published CSA-261162, describing an unknown, likely Chinese-speaking actor that targeted several South Korean financial organizations starting in late September 2026, which is the same period during which we were attacked. "That actor used ARTEX, an open-source Chinese-developed agentic penetration-testing tool released in July 2026, which was also observed to be used in the attack that targeted us." The GoDaddy-owned registrar reported the attack to law enforcement agencies, brought in outside cybersecurity support, and notified the FTC, as well as the data protection authorities in the UK and EU. The company spokesperson added that it worked with Singapore-based ISPs to shut down the attacker's servers in the region, which helped disrupt the attack, in addition to "other actions by us and industry partners." 123 Reg's email to customers stated the attacker's activity "was limited to reading" customer data, although the spokesperson told us "it's possible they created copies of the information," and that this is what prompted the notification. item.title: How Can Africans Advance Cross-Country Equity and Opportunities Through AI?
item.description: Photo source: Goalkeepers 2026 Report For years, Africans have explored how to connect seamlessly without hurdles. As several opportunities are being explored through AI, Africans are also exploring whether AI can be used to advance cross-country opportunities and equity. If it can, what would it look like? What are the initial challenges that can hinder it from happening? What can governments and organisations do to enhance it? Artificial intelligence is changing how people learn, work, build businesses and access information. For young Africans, what opportunities does it present to solve problems, develop new skills and participate in an economy that is becoming increasingly digital? How can those opportunities be available to everyone in the same way? A young person with reliable internet access, a laptop and access to AI training has an advantage over someone who lacks these resources. The gap widens further when we consider young people across countries with different levels of digital infrastructure and investment. If AI is to improve the lives of African youth, access to its benefits must extend beyond the countries and communities already positioned to take advantage of it. African countries need to work together, share resources and invest in solutions that respond to the needs of their people. Bill Gates in Rwanda. Photo by Jean Biziman for Gates Foundation One area, and perhaps the most important area, where this cooperation matters is language. There are thousands of languages spoken in Africa. But much of the technology used to develop AI relies on data in widely spoken languages (in many cases in Africa, English and French), leaving many African languages underrepresented. This limits who can use these tools and how useful they can be. For a young person who speaks an African language but struggles with English or French, AI may not offer the same opportunities it offers someone who is fluent in these languages. The Masakhane research community is working to address this problem by developing natural language processing technologies for African languages. The community consists of Africans representing different languages across Africa. It is an example of what can happen when African researchers collaborate to make technology more inclusive. Through initiatives such as the Masakhane AI Languages Hub, researchers can develop datasets across 40 African languages to support the creation of more useful AI tools. In the 2026 Goalkeepers Report , Bill Gates said AI must b e able to work in every language spoken to create significant equality. Goalkeepers 2026 Report African countries can build on this work by investing in shared language resources, supporting local researchers and making datasets available for responsible use. Instead of each country working independently on similar challenges, regional partnerships could help researchers share knowledge and develop tools that serve communities across borders. This could make it easier

item.title: Open Cosmos steps up Europe's space sovereignty game, shows off ConnectedCosmos satellites
item.description: The question of who controls satellite-based connectivity came into sharp focus in recent weeks after Ukraine's service was throttled and then restored. Wherever Reg readers stand on those activities involving SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield, reliance on a foreign power that may not stay friendly is now under intense scrutiny. Alternatives exist, including Eutelsat OneWeb's constellation, and more are in the works. The Register toured the Harwell facility of another contender – Open Cosmos. The business is just over a decade old and operates from multiple locations, including the UK, Greece, and Portugal. It has launched dozens of missions over the years, including its OpenConstellation service, which organizations use to share data from Earth observation satellites. When it launched OpenConstellation in 2022 , the aim was to have 25 satellites offering a mix of spatial and spectral resolution. While other services, such as the European Commission's Copernicus, provide similar data, OpenConstellation lets customers assign satellites specific tasks for specific data collection. However, it is ConnectedCosmos that will interest users concerned about putting all their connectivity eggs in a basket that might be abruptly snatched away. The first two satellites in the constellation are now in orbit; they were launched by Rocket Lab in January 2026. The business plans to operate more than 96 satellites by the end of 2028 and to achieve full coverage by 2030. The core connectivity backbone will consist of 192 satellites, which founder and CEO Rafel Jordà Siquier described as "the foundation, not the ceiling." The company reckons it can churn out one satellite per day, and judging by what we saw in Harwell, that figure seems realistic, though it's a far cry from the approximately 70 Starlinks per week SpaceX claimed in its IPO filing . Because ConnectedCosmos operates from an altitude above 1,000 km, it needs far fewer satellites, though at the cost of latency increases. Jordi Barrera Ars, co-founder and CTO, told us that latency was "anything between 30 and 80 milliseconds." This is OK for most applications, but not great for some. Direct to smartphone is, for example, not currently on the cards. Open Cosmos's VP of Commercial Satcom, Danielle Edwards, said, "We're very much in the direct device business. Direct to smartphone is not an area that we have an interest in right now." "Never say never…" she added, "and who knows what might come along next Tuesday. But for right now, the direct device play really is on the IoT side." During the tour, Open Cosmos showed off its assembly and testing facilities (including temperature and pressure testing), as well as a shaker table that simulates launch conditions. The satellites themselves consist of a common bus, onto which solar panels and the payload are fitted. Then they are stored, ready for launch, in what one company representative called "the satellite nursery". The approach is interesting: OpenConstel

item.title: Taiwo Awoniyi Honoured with ‘Beyond the Pitch’ Award at the 2026 Best of Africa Awards in London
item.description: Taiwo Awoniyi posing on the red carpet at the Best of Africa Awards 2026 in London. Nigerian international striker Taiwo Awoniyi has picked up the prestigious ‘Beyond the Pitch’ Award at the 2026 Best of Africa Awards in London, marking a major moment of recognition for his work both on and off the football field. Known for his clinical goalscoring ability and strength upfront, the Nottingham Forest and Super Eagles forward plays as a central striker at the highest level of European football. Beyond his professional career in the English Premier League, Taiwo has consistently directed his resources towards community development, healthcare support, and youth empowerment in Nigeria—most notably through his funding and sponsorship of the Kwara Kiddies League, an initiative providing structured grassroots football opportunities for young talents in Kwara State. The Best of Africa Awards, held annually in London, celebrate the outstanding contributions of African figures and individuals of African heritage across sports, entertainment, and social impact. Supported by the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA), the ‘Beyond the Pitch’ accolade specifically highlights athletes who use their global platform to drive tangible social change and uplift their home communities. Taking to Instagram to reflect on the honour, Taiwo shared a message with his followers: Life can give you so much, but what truly matters is what you choose to do with what you’ve been given. Grateful to receive the PFA Beyond the Pitch Award at the Best of Africa Awards 2026. His philanthropic commitments include fully funding the annual Kwara Kiddies League tournament, providing kits, equipment, and cash prizes for grassroots teams across Ilorin and surrounding areas to help young footballers build sustainable career pathways. Taiwo Awoniyi holding his PFA Beyond the Pitch Award trophy at the Best of Africa Awards 2026. *** Photo Credit: Taiwo Awoniyi/Instagram The post Taiwo Awoniyi Honoured with ‘Beyond the Pitch’ Award at the 2026 Best of Africa Awards in London appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Man spends 35 years collecting corporatespeak, turns it into an app
item.description: After suffering more than 10,000 corporate meetings, one executive has decided that the world hasn't endured nearly enough management jargon and built an app capable of generating 270 million variations of it. Dave Doty, who claims to have spent 35 years collecting buzzwords, clichés, and other verbal atrocities inflicted on office workers, turned his life's work into Executive Eightball, an iPhone and Android app designed to help users sound convincingly corporate while saying nothing. The idea came about after Doty spent decades recording the nonsense he heard in meetings, presumably while everyone else was busy circling back, touching base, and taking things offline. "I am an executive who has suffered through over 10,000 meetings during the course of my 30-year career," Doty told The Register . "To keep my sanity, in each of them, I wrote down all of the buzz words and business clichés and have built an enormous database of them." He described his creation as "sort of what would happen if Dilbert and George Costanza had a love child." The app, which is now available on Apple's App Store and Google Play, takes Doty's collection of corporate waffle and assembles it into sentences that wouldn't look out of place in a CEO's quarterly update or a particularly painful all-hands meeting. Among the pearls of wisdom it can produce are "We must dashboard the outputs to enable us to focus on operational directives and break the paradigm" and "Drive to cross-functional synergies so we can reengineer the organization and unleash shareholder value." Doty claims Executive Eightball can produce approximately 270 million unique sentences in 15 languages, meaning workers across the globe can now contribute to meetings without the tiresome business of having an actual idea. The app's listing promises to help users "Speak fluent corporate nonsense instantly," with suggested applications including office humor, LinkedIn jokes, presentation icebreakers, and, perhaps most appropriately, "Fake CEO energy." There's a free version, although you'll have to put up with ads and a limited supply of corporate waffle. For $0.99, you can unlock the lot and talk complete rubbish to your heart's content. The timing is rather fitting. In March, research covered by The Register suggested that people who enthusiastically embrace corporate buzzwords may actually be worse at their jobs. Now there's an app to help the rest of us catch up. Doty, meanwhile, appears delighted with his contribution to the corporate world. "This is truly a paradigm shift for corporate leadership and my greatest lifetime contribution to society," he wrote in his latest email, urging potential customers to subscribe to the paid version to "unleash the value." After 35 years and 10,000 meetings, at least someone has finally found a productive use for all that wasted time. ®

item.title: Black holes can split in two — but only if they spin at extreme speeds
item.description: null Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves. Now, new research suggests that the opposite may happen, too: single black holes may be able to split in two. But this can only happen if that progenitor black hole is spinning at maximum possible speed. That speed prevents the black holes from immediately falling back on each other. There are physical laws in place that would usually prevent black holes from splitting in two; the team behind this research investigated whether there are conditions in which these laws can be temporarily bypassed. One of the key aspects of physics that prevents black holes from bifurcating comes from thermodynamics . Black holes possess a characteristic called " entropy ," which is essentially a measure of disorder within a system. Imagine a toddler's crayon box. When entropy is low, the crayons are neatly arranged by color. As entropy is increased, the crayons are scattered and no longer in order. To get the crayons back in order, it requires a parent to put energy into the system and neatly reorder the crayons. In other words, the entropy of a system can't be reduced without some intervention and energy being added from outside that system. Parenting would be a little easier if it could. A black hole splitting in two would represent a decrease in entropy, strongly disfavored by the laws of thermodynamics, but only if the black hole is not rotating. The situation could be different for a rapidly rotating black hole. This team of scientists found that a loophole exists for such a black hole. "The two resulting black holes must also be able to separate rather than immediately fall back together," team member Francesco Sannino of the University of Naples Federico II in Italy said in a statement . "When we include this requirement, the window largely closes again, except possibly for black holes rotating close to their maximum possible rate." Black hole trousers? The team calculated just how such a black hole split could occur, finding that the division of the black hole's outer boundary, or "event horizon," proceeds in an oddly trouser-like shape, with one resulting black hole slipping down each "leg." They termed this "pair-of-pants topologies." The researchers also determined that a split is more likely to take place if one of the resultant black holes is considerably smaller than its newly born twin. An illustration of a black hole splitting in two, creating the shape of pants. (Image credit: Francesco Sannino) "We cannot yet give a single probability for a black hole to split. It depends on how gravity behaves beyond Einstein's theory , and we are working to quantify this," Sannino said. "We expect small primordial black holes to be more prone to splitting than much larger astrophysical black holes." Sannino added that such black hole s

item.description: Heineken returns to Lagos Fashion Week from October 29 to 31, 2026, continuing a decade-long partnership that has evolved beyond sponsorship into a platform for creative collaboration, cultural expression and shared experiences. Through City of Cities: Where Taste Rules , Heineken will celebrate the people, cultures and creative expressions shaping Lagos, bringing its presence to life across the Heineken Lounge, Heineken Runway Showcase, Heineken Studio and the After Party. First introduced in Lagos in 2025, City of Cities: Where Taste Rules celebrates the diversity that defines the city, where different cultures, styles, communities and perspectives converge. From fashion and music to food, art and social experiences, Lagos draws its character from the people and influences that shape it. For Heineken, this reflects the many ways taste is expressed, experienced and shared. Over the past decade, Heineken’s partnership with Lagos Fashion Week has evolved through initiatives that explore the relationship between fashion, craftsmanship and taste. From the sustainable fashion focus of Woven Threads in 2022 and the Dyelab collaboration in 2023 to the H45 Collection in 2024 and the introduction of City of Cities: Where Taste Rules in 2025, each chapter has offered a distinct expression of the partnership. In 2026, Heineken continues this legacy, creating new opportunities to connect with the people, ideas and experiences shaping contemporary Nigerian fashion and culture. This year’s Heineken Lagos Fashion Week theme, CRAFTED , provides a natural context for this next chapter, celebrating intentionality, artistry, craftsmanship and more considered approaches to fashion and sustainability. Reflecting this spirit, Heineken will bring its presence to life across the week through the Heineken Lounge, the Cruise Collection runway, Heineken Studio and the Heineken Studio After Party, creating experiences that extend beyond the runway. Making its Nigerian debut, Heineken Studio introduces a new dimension to the brand’s exploration of taste and innovation. Described as Heineken’s Playground of Innovation, Studio explores new ways to serve and experience lager through experimentation, brewer expertise and discovery. Experiences such as Foam Infusions will invite guests to discover unexpected flavour combinations, bringing a fresh perspective to taste within the wider Heineken Lagos Fashion Week experience. Speaking on the experience, Sandra Amachree , Head of Marketing and Communications at Nigerian Breweries , said: “For a decade, our partnership with Heineken Lagos Fashion Week has been a meaningful expression of Heineken’s connection to fashion, creativity and culture. item.title: Neocloud thinks AI agents - not meatbags - will be its main customers
item.description: Newly formed Quake AI is a cloud provider that expects its users will be mostly agents rather than humans. It was created after US-based Rumble Inc acquired German datacenter operator Northern Data in June. The parent then rebranded as RUM Group, a holding company for Quake AI (formerly Northern Data) and the Rumble video platform. Quake AI is an Nvidia Cloud Partner (NCP) operating a 22,000 GPUs estate, making it a neocloud: a specialized infrastructure provider dedicated to AI workloads. Yet where other neoclouds are building a full stack of services around their GPU farms, Quake AI wants to make its infrastructure discoverable to AI agents, which may soon be traversing the internet in hordes on behalf of their owners. RUM Group's chief financial officer Mike Masci told The Register that "Cloud 1.0 - let's call it applications - is like a user interface of how you interact with a machine of some kind." He added: "Now, if you think about agents, they don't use vision. That's not how they interact with systems. They interact with APIs and with information effectively, and that means they want highly discoverable, highly data-driven platforms.. “So, to us, the things that make GPUs and AI compute easier to consume for humans, things like model-as-a-service, dashboards and one-click settings, are actually orthogonal to, if not detrimental to what agents are going to want, agents are going to want homogeneous compute… to understand and know what your data and your expectations are in terms of performance and uptimes, and then they're going to want to consume that compute as a utility,” he claimed. In other words, Quake AI believes that, at some point, the customers for its compute services are going to be AI agents rather than people, but carrying out tasks on their behalf. “I think that is the case, and it's the vision that we are driving towards, and you know ultimately agents are in service of people, right?” Masci said. In its view of things, agents won't go through an intermediary, they'll go to the compute to retrieve the answers they need. "So all of these tool frameworks and all of these things that we have set up, I think, are a hindrance or an encumbrance to what the agents are going to want to consume, which is a utility," he explained. "Yes, we're a little crazy in this regard," Masci added. "It's different. But I think our worldview is very grounded in the data and the realities. Like, we're a technical team. We understand the engineering, and at the end of the day, I think that most would validate our hypothesis," he continued. John Hoffman, CEO of Northern Data and acting CEO of Quake AI, compared this with a solution he had been shown of an AI that was developed to navigate the internet by itself. "I told it I wanted pizza. It went on to DoorDash's website. Typed pizza in the search box, clicked on the pizza with the highest ranking, went to add to order, knows I like pepperoni, and it clicked through all of this," he said. "Don't ge

item.title: Why roaming packages have become an anachronism in the age of app-first travel
item.description: Travelling in the modern day and age differs significantly from what it looked like a few short decades ago. Today, it is all about apps: you need applications for navigation, booking accommodation, buying tickets for events, following the local news, staying in touch with friends and family, and more. That also means that you depend on connectivity at all times while abroad. The problem is that a lot of people still rely on traditional roaming, while the roaming model is out of date. You cannot choose a specific mobile internet plan that suits your travel plans. Instead, operators have split the world into zones, and each zone has its own pricing, limits, and permissions. That is why many have turned to alternative ways of staying connected, and so far, the travel eSIM has emerged as the most practical solution. Companies like the Swiss eSIM pioneer, Yesim , have recognized the problem that travelers are facing and have come up with a solution. They let you pick a specific plan that will fit your trip. That way, you get to tailor your connectivity experience in advance. Furthermore, you even get to see the price in advance and know exactly what you will have to pay. Home-operator roaming: Connectivity under outdated rules The problem with roaming is that your home operator decides what your internet will be like abroad. When you try to book a flight or a hotel room, you will try to get the best deal possible. That means comparing providers, prices, any potential benefits that different providers offer, and the like. However, with roaming, you can’t do any of that. The terms of your existing home contract still apply, and connectivity abroad just gets added to it. That means that your operator decides what zones are available, what partner networks you can access, and, most importantly, how much they will charge you. You, as the user, can only accept their terms or choose to look for a different way to secure an internet connection. In other words, there is no flexibility and no participation on your end, you can only take it or leave it. Take EE as an example - the official terms for their EE Travel Data pass for Canada and the US say that the user gets 500 MB of data per day. This is not nearly enough for someone who will depend on their phone for everything, from paying for food to comparing ticket prices and booking accommodation. The limit is the same for countless other countries, including Australia, China, India, Mexico, New Zealand, South Africa, Thailand, Turkey, and the UAE. It gets even worse for other countries, including Japan, Singapore, South Korea, and Indonesia. For these, the daily allowance is only 150 MB. That essentially forces you to ration your data use very carefully and pick what you are going to use it for. Some providers have introduced daily packages as a secondary roaming option. item.title: Lagos Fashion Week 2026 Kicks Off Today! Dates, Venue, Designers & What to Wear
item.description: Lagos Fashion Week street style features showing tiered ruffles, tailored white co-ords, and structured Aso-Oke dresses. Clear your schedules and start ironing out those statement fits— Lagos Fashion Week 2026 officially starts today! From Wednesday, 28th October to Sunday, 1st November 2026, the fashion capital of Africa transforms into a high-energy hub of runway shows, street style spectacles, and creative exchanges. Organised by Style House Files, Africa’s premier fashion platform is back to connect local designers, international buyers, media, and style lovers from across the globe. The theme for the 2026 season is “CRAFTED: Heritage. Innovation. Circular Futures.” This year focuses heavily on pushing sustainable, locally rooted craft straight into the global spotlight. Through initiatives like Green Access and the Fashion Business Series, the event highlights zero-waste tailoring, circular design, and modern interpretations of traditional African textiles—from handwoven Aso-Oke and Akwete to indigo-dyed Adire. Whether you are pulling up to the tents in person or following every outfit update online, this complete guide breaks down everything happening this season—from venue details and designer expectations to the street style cues you need to know. Runway mainstays like Lisa Folawiyo , Andrea Iyamah , Ejiro Amos Tafiri , Ugo Monye , Fruché , and Abiola Olusola will be delivering season-defining moments alongside coveted labels like Christie Brown , Cute Saint , Bloke , and Emmy Kasbit . Meanwhile, the Green Access cohort will present sustainable, forward-thinking mini-collections that show how the next generation of African designers is tackling circular fashion. Rather than standard catwalks, several offsite and tent presentations will also showcase raw fabric production, live artisan weaving, and intricate beadwork. Street style stars, content creators,and fashion editors bring their absolute best to Victoria Island. item.title: SK Hynix says memory shortages to persist until 2030
item.description: Korean memory-maker SK Hynix has predicted memory shortages will persist until at least the year 2030 and says that will help it to boost its already exceptional revenue and profits to new levels. In remarks published on Wednesday alongside its quarterly results, the company offered its belief that “a virtuous cycle has taken hold in which AI-driven productivity gains and new revenue generation in areas such as software development, customer service, and search lead to greater AI adoption, which in turn drives increased investment in infrastructure.” SK Hynix thinks this is great news, because it means more buyers are entering the market for AI infrastructure, including “general enterprises” and nations building sovereign infrastructure. In coming years, the company sees even more demand for memory coming from autonomous cars and the growing robotics market. While the company is working hard to build more factories and get them working, execs admitted it can’t do that fast enough to meet demand. “The company assessed that supply … is not keeping pace with the growth of the market,” SK Hynix told investors. “Given technical difficulty of leading-edge processes and the long lead time required to build new production facilities, it expects the structure in which demand exceeds supply to persist through 2030.” It gets worse. SK Hynix has 14 long-term deals with 14 big buyers, who will collectively buy more than half of its output during 2027 and 2028, and some of them want to extend those agreements. The Korean giant doesn’t mind that because the deals include “a mechanism that reflects market conditions within a price range agreed upon with customers” and give it “a structure that secures stable profitability while allowing flexible responses to market changes.” Those deals helped SK Hynix to record quarterly revenue of ₩104.6 trillion ($78.1 billion), up 328 percent year-over-year and 32 percent quarter-over-quarter. Operating profit came in at ₩87.68 trillion ($62.8 billion), up 486 percent year over year. The company told investors it’s not done yet, outlining plans to expand production and emphasize lucrative products that will “scale up revenue and profit one step further next year.” Doing so will likely dent profits elsewhere, because on the company’s earnings call, chief financial officer Kim Woo-hyun predicted “shipment volumes for PCs and mobile devices are expected to decrease due to cost burdens from rising memory prices and supply shortages.” The company also outlined some of its future plans, among them: Increasing HBM4 production, which it believes will “surpass HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter and … establish itself as a mainstream product.” “Rapidly” increasing the portion of its 10nm-class 6th generation (1c) process technology and expand sales of DDR5 and LPDDR5 SOCAMM for AI servers. item.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
item.description:
Dr. Michaela Musilova is an award-winning astrobiologist, explorer, professional speaker and author. Michaela has been conducting space-related research at institutions around the world, including NASA, ESA, CalTech, the Canada-France-Hawaii telescope and many others. She was the Commander of 40 simulated missions to the Moon and Mars — the most missions led to date.

Currently, Michaela is the President and Founder of the nonprofit XtremeFrontiers. She is pioneering a unique global project: Astro Seven Summits. It's a world-first in combining expeditions to the highest mountain on each continent with scientific research in collaboration with NASA and institutions worldwide, educational activities and filming documentaries.

Michaela is also a consultant for numerous companies across the globe for topics ranging from Mars missions all the way to museum exhibitions, such as for the Smithsonian. She is one of very few people to have ever led research projects on all seven continents.

Michaela’s work has been recognized through numerous awards, such as Forbes 30 Under 30, Top 100 Women in Aerospace and Aviation, and the Emerging Space Leaders Grant.

Michaela is regularly invited to give keynote presentations and performs a variety of outreach activities globally as a science communicator. She has been giving interviews to international media for over 20 years, writing scientific and educational articles, and she co-authored her biography, "Woman from Mars."

I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments. Being underwater, if we encountered a major problem with our gear, we would have had to treat it as seriously as if we were astronauts on the International Space Station . There was no immediate "out." This was serious. Before this underwater mission, I had worked as the commander of nearly 40 analog missions that simulated crewed missions to the moon and Mars . The goal of these types of missions is to test what living and working in lunar or Martian environments might be like. We study everything from the psychology of living in extreme conditions, or in isolation, to the technology that astronauts might use to complete those missions successfully. item.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
item.description: null Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf. But on rare occasions, the supernova doesn't completely destroy the star, and a shattered stellar body remains, called a zombie star. These events are called Type Iax supernovas . Pa 30 was first identified in 2013 by a citizen scientist in 2013, but scientists soon linked it to a cosmic explosion recorded independently in the year 1181 in Japanese, Chinese, and Arabic historical documentation. That makes this one of only five supernovas seen before the invention of the telescope. "Reliable historical records of stellar explosions extend back only about a thousand years. For all we know, there might well be similar remnants still lurking in the dark in our own galaxy," team member Ilaria Caiazzo, assistant professor at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA), said in a statement . "Today, we are lucky to study an intriguing object we know was observed by astronomers who made three independent historical records of the event centuries before the invention of the telescope." Solar system-sized pearls Pa 30 is a good laboratory to study supernovas because, at around 7,500 light-years away, it is relatively close to Earth on cosmic scales. For instance, the heart of our galaxy is around 26,000 light-years away. "We can see this much detail because of Pa 30's proximity to Earth," said Caiazzo. "This proximity makes Pa 30 uniquely valuable for study." It is also an important subject of study because it is the only supernova remnant in which we can see a zombie star. Using the Gemini North telescope, Caiazzo and colleagues zoomed in on Pa 30, discovering knots along the strands of gas radiating out from the site of the cosmic explosion, like pearls on a string. These pearls are each wide enough to encompass the orbit of Neptune , the most distant planet from the sun, ten times over. "The planetary region of our solar system could fit in each knot about ten times with room to spare," said Caiazzo. "The knots are quite strikingly uniform. We are excited to try to model them." The team also discovered that the zombie star sits almost perfectly at the heart of Pa 30. When these cosmic explosions happen, they should provide any debris, including zombie stars, with a kick. item.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
item.description: null The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit. The proximity can make a supermoon appear 14% larger and 30% brighter than the smallest full moon of the year, according to NASA . When to see the November full moon The November full moon will be below the horizon for stargazers in the U.S. when it turns full at 9:53 a.m. EST on Nov. 24. Instead, viewers in America will get their best view of the near-full Beaver Moon as it arcs towards the western horizon in the predawn hours of Nov. 23. You may notice the lunar disk take on a gorgeous yellow-orange hue in the hour before moonset, as the bluer wavelengths of its light are scattered by Earth's dense atmosphere through a process known as Rayleigh scattering — the same phenomenon that turns the sky red at sunset. The Beaver Moon glows between the towers of the Benedictine Abbey in the city of Krakow, Poland. (Image credit: Photo by Omar Marques/Anadolu via Getty Images) November's supermoon may appear even larger as it travels close to the horizon thanks to a phenomenon known as the " Moon Illusion ", which tricks us into thinking that the lunar disk is larger than it actually is while closer to foreground objects, compared to when it shines overhead. The moon will also appear fully lit to the casual observer on the evenings of Nov. 23 and Nov. 24, so there's no need to miss out if you struggle with early mornings! The table below details local full moon timings for when the moon is 100% illuminated for a selection of cities spread across the globe (local moonset and moonrise times will vary based on your location): Local full moon timings for November 2026 Local full moon timings for November 2026 City Local time New York 9:53 a.m. EST on Nov. 24 London 2:53 p.m. GMT on Nov. 24 Beijing 10:53 p.m. CST on Nov. 24 Tokyo 11:53 p.m. JST on Nov. 24 Sydney 1:53 a.m. AEDT on Nov. 25 Why it's called the Beaver Moon The November full moon is often called the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time that beavers retreat to their lodges after collecting enough food to see them through the winter.
